cells.date: Šaka 1482, Raudri, Vaiśākha, śu. 15 = 1560 A.D., May 9, Thursday.
cells.reference: ARSIE. , 1915, No. 543,  SII , IX, pt. II, No. 671
cells.object: On a slab in the courtyard of the Kēśavasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: States that the province of Ādavāni-sīme was granted by the king as amara-magaṇi to mahāmaṇdalēśvara Veṅkaṭādrirāja-ayya of the lunar race, and registers a gift of land to the temple of Ahōbala Nārasimhadēva at Būdūru which was given as amara-māgaṇi to mahāmaṇdalēśvara Gōbūri Avubhaṭarājaya, as umbaļi . The gift is stated to have been made on the eve of a lunar eclipse. But such an eclipse occurred only in the month of Phālguṇa of the year Siddhārthi (1560 A.D., Mach 12, Tuesday). Perhaps the record was engraved on the given date.

cells.date: Šaka 14[82], Kāļayukta, Āśvīja, śu. [14], lunar eclipse = 1558 A.D., September 27, Tuesday. The Šaka year was 1480.
cells.object: On a slab near the  garuṭa-stambha  in front of the Aṇjanēyasvāmin temple.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of income from tolls due from the agrahāra Dayyamdinna alias Kṛishṇāpura to the hill fortress of Ādavāni, in favour of the maṭha of Parāṇkuśa Śrī Śathagōpa-jīyamgāru, a Śrīvaishṇava teacher who held the titles Sarvatantrasvatantra and Ubhayavēdāntāchārya . cells.date: Šaka 1454, Nandana, Phālguṇa, ba. 7, Monday = 1533 A.D., March 17.
cells.reference: TLIMP. , I, No. 19;  ARSIE. , 1915, No. 492;  SII. , IX, Pt. II, No. 554.
cells.object: On the east wall of the Āñjanēya temple
cells.remarks: Records the migration of the people of Kavatāļ-sīme to Masaveya-sīme to escape from the tyranny of the palace officials ( aramaneyavaru avanāyava māđalāgi ) and their return to Kavatāļa, at the invitation of the mahāmaṇdalēśvara Salakayadēva Chika Tirumalarāja-mahā-arasa on promise of relief. The terms of the order granting relief are set forth in detail. Accordingly, the agriculturists, fishermen, oil-mongers, potters, washermen etc., were shown several concessions in repayment of taxes, tolls and the like. For this purpose, the chief is stated to have gone to Ādavāni. The record was written by Mallaya of Kaṇiyakallu and engraved by Rāmōja, son of Peruvōja.

cells.date: Śaka 14[6]5, Šubhakṛit, Kārttika, śu. 11 = 1542 A.D., October 19, Thursday.
cells.reference: ARSIE. , 1915, No. 554; SII., IX pt. II, No. 604.
cells.object: On a slab near the eastern wall of Kanuma Dođđayya's temple
cells.remarks: The Śaka year would be 1464. Records that mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Rāmarāja Kōnēṭi Timmayadēva-mahā-arasu made a gift of gold out of the income of bēđike , birāđa and the like in the village Kōṭeyakallu situated in Ādavāni-vaļita which had been granted to him by the king for his chieftaincy ( nāyakatana ), and a plot of land, for the service of god Hanumantadēva at Kōṭeyakallu and for the tīrtha-chhatra . The gift was made for the merit of the king and for the attainment of vaikuṇṭha for the donor's ancestors. Ādavāni-vaļita is stated to have been a division of Hastināvati in Mūđa-nāđu.

cells.object: On a pillar in the Lakshmi temple

cells.date: Śaka 1470, Kīlaka, Āshaḍha, śu.  prathama-dvādaśi , Sunday = 1548 A.D., June 17.
cells.object: On the copper-plates received from the Collector of Anantapur.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Kanuma, by the king, to several learned Brāhmaṇas of various gōtras and śākhas . The grant was made at the request of Appalarāja, son of Kṛishṇarāya and grandson of Timmarāja of Kāśyapānvaya. The village Kanuma was situated in Muṇḍimadugu-sīme, of Gutti-vaļita. The village granted is divided equally between god Chennakēśava at Muṇḍimaḍugu on the bank of the river Pinākini and the Brāhmaṇas. One half is left as the temple property. The other portion was split into 30 vṛittis and keeping 2 vṛittis for the daily worship of the god, the remaining were distributed among the Brāhmaṇas, who were required to perform sixteen kinds of service ( shōdaśōpachāra ) to the deity. The gift was made on the bank of the Tuṅgabhadrā, in the presence of god Viṭṭhalēśvara.

cells.date: Śaka 15[39], Piñgaļa = 1617-18 A.D.
cells.object: On a rock south of the village
cells.remarks: Damaged. Refers to the rule at Kalyāṇadurga, of a certain Veňkaṭapati-nāyanayyavāru, son of Rā ya-daļavā yi Kōnēṭi-nāyuđu and to the gift of the village Kottapalle to a certain Dāsappa-nāyuđu as a feudal tenure ( pāļepaṭtu ). cells.date: Šaka 1095 , Śrīmukha , Āśvīja , ba. 12. The details are wrong.
cells.object: On the copper-plates received from the Gārachāvađi Pullayya , Clerk , Fund Office Kannada and Telugu
cells.remarks: Purports to record a similar grant by the king , of the dēsāhi-karaṇika right over the vaļitas of Tummala , Kanagānipalle , Pappūru and Yāđiki (villages) to Mallarasu , son of Nāgarasu and grandson of Vīrarasu of the Kauṇđinya-gōtra. The grant is said to have been made for the merit of Virūpākshēśvara in the presence of Kriyāśaktisvāmi. The villages of Velpumađugu in the Tummala-sīma and Mālyavantam in the Pappūru-sīma were each renamed as Prauđhadēvarāyapuram. The officer was given lands in several places as remuneration. This also appears to be spurious. The date given is far too early for the king.

cells.date: Šaka 1455, Vijaya, Kārttika, śu. 12, Wednesday,  Utthāna-dvādaśi  = 1533 A.D., October 29.
cells.reference: AR. , 59 of 1912;  TLIMP. , I, No. 10;  SII. , XVI, No. 106.
cells.object: On a slab in the village
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of some wet lands constituted into a hamlet called Mallapanāyanipalli, in Dharmāvaram, to god Maṇđem Nārasimhadēva, who was pleased to manifest himself in the field near Dharmāvaram, by mahāmaṇdalēśvara Salakarāju China Tirumalayyadēva-mahārāju, who led the Tiruvađi campaign and was a brother-in-law and minister of the king. The gift was made for the merit of his parents Salakarāju and Tipājamma. The donor is said to have obtained Dharmavaram as nāyaṅkara from the king.

cells.object: Copper-plate obtained through the Tahsildar of Dharmavaram
cells.remarks: This spurious charter states that Bhōgi-nāyuḍu, Jikka-nāyuḍu, Jyōti-nāyuḍu and Aṇṇa Chennama-nāyuḍu, sons of mahānāyaṇkāchārya.yākali Vīra Bhōgi-nāyuḍu, having settled Nāgi-ređđi and Nārappa-ređđi, son of Vōbi-ređđi, with half a share, and Kṛishṇa-ređđi and Veṇkaṭa-ređđi, sons of Nāgi-ređđi with the other half share in Dharmavaram, the latter in turn settled several families of various professions such as the priest, the carpenter, the mason, etc. by gifts of land in the gift village. The tank and the temple of Chennakēśava at Dharmavaram are said to have been constructed by Chikka-vođeya of Ānegoṇđi.

cells.remarks: Damaged. cells.remarks: States that Sāļuva Timmarasayya granted the village Arasinēnipalli to god Tirumaladēva of Bētapalli and that after some time a certain Yaramarāja purchased the village; but the latter's father mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Vuyalavađa Chūļappa-nāyaka disapproving this transaction of his son, as that village was already endowed to the god, made over the village for the benefit of the god and the servants of the temple were permitted to have their shares of income out of it as usual. This rearrangement was made for the merit of Salakarāju Peda Tirumalarāja, when the region was bestowed (as mānya ) on him by the king. This seems to be identical with No. AP 96 above.

cells.date: Šaka 1439, Īśvara = 1517-18 A.D.
cells.reference: ARSIE. , 87 of 1912;  Ins. Mad. , I, No. 47
cells.object: On a slab in the courtyard of the Chauđēśvari temple
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Records a gift to the Chauđēśvari temple at Chōļasamudra by rāyasam Koņđamarasayya, son of Timmarasa-mantri, who was one of the sons of Šrīpatyā-chārya, chief of Podaṭuru in Drāviđa-dēśa and the ornament of the Udayagiri Kannađiga sect. The gift was made in order that the king may be blessed with children. (Koņđamarasayya is said to have actually planted the Vijayanagara colours on the Simhādri and Šrīkurmam during the king's celebrated campaign in the north. It is thought it was evidently after this that Tirumala was born. Anyhow, according to this record Koņđamarasayya would be the son of Timmarasa and grandson of Šrīpatyāchārya. This last had other sons besides Timmarasa.)

cells.date: Šaka 14 ..... ba. 7
cells.reference: ARSIE. , 1920, No. 408;  SII. , IX, pt. II, No. 681
cells.object: On a stone in front of the Chennakēśava temple
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records that, unable to bear the enhanced and numerous taxes, the people of the village Chebale had deserted it and that daļavāyi Appala-nāyaka, agent of Koņđaiyadēva-mahā-arasu, to whom the district containing the village was given as amaramāgaṇi invited the people and persuaded them to resettle in the village giving them some concessions. The concessions were: (1) that they need not pay for three years sēnabōva-varttane , rāyasa-varttane , fees to royal servants, kāṇike , kađāya , cess on marriage and other domestic festivals, exempted from free work for the service of god Henneyadeva and other imposts (2) that after three years such taxes as were current elsewhere would be justly levied; (3) and that the rate of the rent payable to the palace would be according to the quality of the soil.

cells.date: Śaka 1469, Plavaṅga, Bhādrapada, śu. 15, Tuesday = 1547 A.D., August 30.
cells.reference: ARSIE. , 384 of 1920;  SII. , IX, pt. II, No. 624
cells.object: On a stone near the well
cells.remarks: Records that at the request of the sons of Puli Appana-bōva of Kasavāpura, which had been granted by Kōnēṭi Timmarājayya, son of Rāmarāja Koṇḍarāja, as an umbaļi to daļavāyi Yallappa-nāyaka, the latter abolished terīge , horīge , kraya , sidhāya , biṭṭi , and birāḍa and other cesses levied upon the fishermen. The capture of cocks and pigs was also prohibited. The exemption was made for the merit of Kōnēṭi Timmarājayya.

cells.date: Šaka 1478, Naļa, Āshāđha, śu. 11 = 1556 A.D., June 18, Thursday.
cells.reference: AR. , 423 of 1920;  SII. , IX, pt. II, No. 663
cells.object: On a slab in the Narasimhasvāmi temple
cells.remarks: Records that Kōnapadēva-mahā-arasu, son of mahāmaṇdalēśvara Rāmarāja Appayyadēva-mahā-arasu, exempted the mahājanas of the agrahāras of Nadale, Nimbegalu, Rāyapanahalli, Kalidīvanahalli, Sirivara, Rēvināyakanahalli, Yaraguđi, Tumbeganūru, Rāghanahāļu, Tāvaregoļa, Chikapēpali, Timmāpura, Hōtūru, Benakanahalli, Añṭarasanahāļu and Kamalahāļu, situated in Uruvakonđe-sīme, a sub-division of Rāyadurga-vēņthe from such taxes as taļavārike , bēđike , rāyasada-vartane , karaṇikara-vartane , talavārike-vartane , yeleya-pammu , maharnavami-ulupe , hennedēvara-ulupe , kammaṭada-kūli , soppe , birāđa , dañđina-kāṇike , janasāle and haraļabhaṭti . The gift was made (including the grāmagrāsa land of Timmāpura given by Timmappa-nāyaka) in the presence of god Narasimhasvāmi of Henne Ahōbaļa on the bank of the river Pinākini, for the merit of the donor's father Appalarājayya and his brother Tirumalarāja.

cells.date: Šaka 1419, Piņgaļa, Chaitra, śu. 9, Saturday,  Šrīrāma-navami  = 1497 A.D., March 13, Monday.
cells.object: Slab in the Rāmēśvara temple
cells.remarks: It registers a gift of the village Jarivūči (Jarivūtļa) situated in Penna-māgaņi of Jagatāpi-Gutti, which was given to him as a nāyaṅkara , to god Rāmayadēva of that place, on the occasion of Šrīrāma-navami , by Kēśama-nāyađu, son of mahānāyaṅkāchārya Janne Chennama-nāyuđu, for the merit of the king and Narasa-nāyaka and his own parents. The gift was made with the permission of the king and in the presence of god Sētubandha Rāmēśvara. The gift was inclusive of all canals, tanks, wells, kāđāramba and the ashṭa-bhōga-tēja-svāmya . From the text it appears as though the gift was made at Sētubandha Rāmēśvara, where he appears to have gone. It was made with the permission of the king who appears to have instructed that for the gift to be eternal, it should be recorded ( śāsanastaṅgā samarpiṇchumani Rāyala nirūpam-valla ).

The gift was made with the permission of the king and in the presence of god Sētubandha Rāmēśvara. The gift was inclusive of all canals, tanks, wells,  kāđāramba  and the  ashṭa-bhōga-tēja-svāmya . From the text it appears as though the gift was made at Sētubandha Rāmēśvara, where he appears to have gone. It was made with the permission of the king who appears to have instructed that for the gift to be eternal, it should be recorded ( śāsanastaṅgā samarpiṇchumani Rāyala nirūpam-valla ).

Refers to Mudda-daṇdanāyaka as the sachiva . The king may be Harihara II.

cells.date: Śaka 1439, Īsvara, Mārgaśira, ba. 2 = 1517 A.D., December 2, Tuesday.
cells.object: On a slab in the courtyard of the Chauđēśvari temple
cells.remarks: Ref.: A.R.Ep. , 1912, No. 87; SII. , IX, pt. II, No. 507 Rāyasada Koṇđamarasayya, son of mantri Timmarasa and grandson of Śrīpatyāchārya, who was the chief of Proddaṭūr in the Drāviḍa-dēśa, granted some gifts for the services of goddess Chauđēśvari in Chōłasamudra, in order that the king may be blessed with children. The king is eulogised as Karnāṭaka-simhāsanārūḍha . Koṇđamarasayya was an expert in reading several scripts ( chhappannadēśa chitralipi lēkha-kōvidam ) while his grandfather is described as the ornament of the kannađiga-kula of Udayagiri ( Udayagiri-kannađiga-kula-tilaka ).

cells.remarks: Ref.: A.R.Ep. , 1965-66, No. A 1; Published in Ep. Ind. Vol. XXXVIII , pt. 111 Copper-plate in the possession of Shri K.A.Nagaraja Rao, Panchayat Board President Sanskrit and Kannada in Nandi-Nāgar Saṅgama; Dēvarāya II Śaka 1339 ( nava-guṇa-rāma-chandra ) (wrong for 1336), Jaya, Phālguṇa ( Tapasya ), śu. 5 (Ishu), Thursday = 1415 A.D., February 14. States that the prince Rāmachandra, on the orders of the king, his father, went on an expedition to Āndhradēśa with his army, visiting en route Śrīgiri (Śrīśailam) where he is said to have consecrated ( i.e. , reconsecrated) god Śiva and his consort near a hill in a forest. His wife Bukkāmbarā, daughter of Aubhalārāja, who was the son of Rudradēva, with the consent of her lord, granted as sarvamānya-agrahāra a village called Kamchikumṭa, after renaming it as Bukkāpura, to be shared by eight Brāhmaṇas of whom Dēvarāya, the composer of the record was one. The date (1415 A.D.) of Rāmachandra's campaign in the Āndhra country would indicate that it was directed against the alliances of Firoz Shah and Peda Kōmaṭi Vēma ( Further Sources , Vol. I, p. 88).

text.remarks: Ref.:  A.R.Ep. , 1965-66, No. A 1; Published in  Ep. Ind. Vol. XXXVIII , pt. 111 Copper-plate in the possession of Shri K.A.Nagaraja Rao, Panchayat Board President Sanskrit and Kannada in Nandi-Nāgar Saṅgama; Dēvarāya II Śaka 1339 ( nava-guṇa-rāma-chandra ) (wrong for 1336), Jaya, Phālguṇa ( Tapasya ), śu. 5 (Ishu), Thursday = 1415 A.D., February 14. States that the prince Rāmachandra, on the orders of the king, his father, went on an expedition to Āndhradēśa with his army, visiting  en route  Śrīgiri (Śrīśailam) where he is said to have consecrated ( i.e. , reconsecrated) god Śiva and his consort near a hill in a forest. His wife Bukkāmbarā, daughter of Aubhalārāja, who was the son of Rudradēva, with the consent of her lord, granted as  sarvamānya-agrahāra  a village called Kamchikumṭa, after renaming it as Bukkāpura, to be shared by eight Brāhmaṇas of whom Dēvarāya, the composer of the record was one. The date (1415 A.D.) of Rāmachandra's campaign in the Āndhra country would indicate that it was directed against the alliances of Firoz Shah and Peda Kōmaṭi Vēma ( Further Sources , Vol. I, p. 88).

cells.object: On the copper-plate received from the Tahsildar
cells.remarks: A plain forgery which pretends to be dated in the reign of Vijaya-Bukkarāya (Śaka 1331 to 1344). Registers the advent of a number of gauṇḍas from Nagara-sīma with their carts ( i.e. , baggage?) to settle in the country ruled by Sōmaśaṅkara-nāyaka of Ratnagiri. Three new villages were founded and village officers appointed. Also mentions Malikībharāma-varaha ( i.e. , pagōḍa issued by the Golcoṇḍa king Malik-Ibrāhim).

cells.date: Śaka 1354, Parīdhāvi, Kārttika, śu. 1, Friday = 1432 A.D., October, Friday, f.d.t. .38
cells.reference: ARSIE. , 1917, No. 765;  SII. , IX, pt. II, No. 443
cells.object: On a Nandi pillar near the Āñjanēya temple
cells.remarks: It records that the king abolished the tax on marriage among all castes in Koṭapi. It also states that those who marry and go out keeping the Basava (on the pillar on which the inscription is engraved) to their right, will be blessed with many children. That this superstitious belief was prevalent then is noteworthy.

cells.object: On the east wall of the second  prākāra  in the same temple

cells.object: On the east wall of the second  prākāra  of the same temple

This village surnamed Virūpāksharāyapura, (near) Kārakalike in Buruḍakuṇṭe-rājya, is stated to have been granted as a mānya to Timmappa's grand-father Viramarasa, by Virūpākshadēva-mahārāya in Śaka 1389, Sarvajit, Pushya, śu. 2, Monday corresponding to 1467 A.D., December 28. The sale price was fixed by the madhyastas . The record is damaged at the end.

cells.object: On the east wall of the second  prākāra  in the same temple
cells.remarks: Records a gift to the shrines of Pāpavināśadēva, Raghunāthadēva and Vīrēśvaradēva by the mahājanas of Nagaragere alias Krīshṇarāyasamudra-agrahāra, a village in Rodda-nāđu, which was a subdivision of Penugoṇđe-rājya. cells.remarks: Penugoṇđe Virūpaṇṇayya, son of Nandi Lakki-seṭṭi and Mudamāmba, purchased the village Chikkanandi-cheṛuvu from certain Brāhmaṇas (named) by paying 400 ghaṭṭi varahas fixed by the mediators (madhyasta-parikalpita-kraya-mūla-dravya) . He made a gift of this village for the service of god Vīrabhadra of Lēpākshi. The gift village (surnamed Dēvarāyapura) near Deppaṛu in Sādali-sthaļa of Chēļūra-chāvađi is stated to have been granted as a sarvamānya originally to an ancestor of these Brāhmaṇas by Prauđhadēva-mahārāya.

cells.location: Mēđiređđipalle (hamlet of Maṇḍalapalle) · Hindupur Taluk · Anantapur
cells.date: Šaka 1309, Prabhava, Māgha, śu. 15, Thursday = 1388 A.D., January 23, Thursday, f.d.t. .00.
cells.object: Slab set up by the road side to the north of the village
cells.remarks: While Bukkarāya, son of Vīra Harihararāya was ruling, mahānāyaṅkāchārya Harigula Kiti-nāyaka's son Poli-nāyaka, administering Mēđiređđipalli, got a channel dug out, from Chilēru to the tank in the village, by Peda Bayirapōja and China Bayirapōja, sons of Tolēți Dēvōja and granted them land below the tank as dasavanda . The extent of the land was siṅgāya tumura pamdumu mađi . The channel was obviously a feeder channel.

cells.date: Śaka 1338 , Hēmaļamba , Plāhguṇa , śu. 15 , Thursday = 1418 A.D. , February 20. But the week-day was Sunday.
cells.object: Slab below a peepul tree in the courtyard of the same temple
cells.remarks: Damaged. States that the merchant coummunity sat in an assembly and heard a representation made by the māla , mādiga and rytus and gave a decision regarding the exemption of pannu due to the māla ( mālavāriki jalle pannu lēkuṇda sūla. . . . ) and other issues the details of which are all lost. In this connection it refers to the observance of the duties of the kula ( kulācharaṇa ). The king is described as Chikkarāya Vīra Kumāra Dēvarāya ( śrī Vīra Harihararāya Chikkarāya Ẹrī Vīra Kumāra Dēvarāya mahārāya ). The merchant community is referred to as the devotees of Dau(Gau)rēśvaradēva having 86 dēśas under their control.

The merchant community is referred to as the devotees of Dau(Gau)rēśvaradēva having 86  dēśas  under their control.

cells.date: Šaka 1444, Chitrabhānu, Pushya, śu. 10, Sunday, Makara-saṭkrānti = 1522 A.D., December 28.
cells.object: On a slab in front of the temple
cells.remarks: Narasa-nāyaka, son of mahānāyaṅkāchārya Kundurupi Timmi-nāyaka made a grant of the village Bhairasamudram in Kugari-nāđu, a subdivision of Kumdurupi which was favoured to his nāyaṅkara by the king at the request of Koṇđamarasayya, in Rāyadurga, for the service of god Tiruveṅgaļanātha of Vēmpalapariti. The gift was a sarvamānya . Some part of the grant was given to Anantappa, son of Rāmayya Anantayya Kuppālamma and grandson of sthānika Kalakađa Channamayya as archanā-vṛitti . The grant was made for the merit of Rāyasam Koṇđamarasayya and Kuṇduripi Timma-nāyaka. This would mean that Rāmayya's son Anantayya's wife was Kuppālamma and their son was Anantappa.

cells.reference: ARSIE. , 1928, No. 23;  SII. , IX, pt. II, No. 688
cells.object: On a slab built into the south wall of the Raṅgasvāmi temple
cells.remarks: Damaged. Refers to the report made by the learned men of Erāguđi, to the east of the Hagare in Vēparāla-vēnṭhe, a subdivision of Rāyadurga-rājya, to the king Šrīraṅgarāya about the gift made to them of the village Šrīraṅgasamudra, during the reign of king Krīshṇarāya, by Šrīraṅgaraya, son of Tirumalanātha of Chaturtha-gōtra, who had also constructed for their use, the temple of Śrīraṅganātha, a tank and a canal connecting the tank with a river for the supply of water and provided for the worship of the god by granting lands to the temple and that those had been ruined by the Turukas. Rest of the record is lost. It mentions Giriyōja of Chennāpuri.

cells.date: Śaka 1420 , Piṅgaļa , Chaitra , śu. 1[5] , Saturday = 1497 A.D. , March 18 , Saturday.
cells.object: On the south wall of the Śaṅkarēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Ref.: A.R.Ep. , 1917 , No. 719; SII. , IX , pt. II , No. 474 Records the grant of a village , Paliganaha!ļi alias Immađi Kāchāpura in Agaļisthaļa of Rāyadurga-chāvađi, to god Śamkara of Agaļi, by Immađi Kāchappa-nāyaka, son of Kāchappa-nāyaka of Ādavāni. The gift was made in the presence of god Rāmēśvara when the donor had gone to Sētubandha Rāmēśvara with Narasaṇṇa-nāyaka. It is stated that Kāchappa-nāyaka held the division of Agaļisthaļa as a fief from Narasiṅgarāya-mahārāya who had bestowed on Narasaṇṇa-nāyaka the Rāyadurga-chāvađi for his nāyakatana . The village granted was resettled ( rūpu-māđi ) by him.

cells.remarks: Registers that, in Śaka 1120, Bhāva (wrong), a certain Bomma-nāyaka with the permission of Harihara-Bukkarāya, appointed kāṇachigāras in the Mādasamudra village which he had founded. Then in Śaka 1223, Naļa (also wrong), in the reign of Bhūpatirāya, son of Harihara Bukkarāya, Bomma's son Kāma-nāyaka founded the village Gövindapura, to the south of Malligemađu, which he renamed Rorļe. The dates are wrong. The year Bhāva corresponded with 1334-35 A.D., while Naļa occurred on 1376-77 A.D., which may be the intended dates.

cells.date: Śaka 1407 , Viśvāvasu , Āśvīja , śu. . . . = 1485 A.D. , September 8 , Thursday on which day a solar eclipse occurred , the  tithi  being Bhādrapada , ba. 15. It is quite likely that the record was engraved on the next day , Āśvīja , śu. 1 , the date corresponding to 1485 A.D. , September 9 , Friday , f.d.t. .06
cells.reference: ARSIE.  , 1917 , No. 710;  SII.  , IX , pt. II , No. 472
cells.remarks: Rāyaparāja , son of Bayarājadēva Chōļa-mahā-arasa made a gift of land and the channel called Śaṅkaradēvana-kāluve to Narasimha-sōmayāji , Prasanna-sōmayāji and Lakshmaṇa-sōmayāji , sons of daśagranthi Narasimha-sōmayāji of Āśvalāyanasūtra, Kāśyapa-gōtra and Rik-śākha, on the condition that they would convert the valley adjoining the field into a tank and call it Narasāmbudhi after the king Narasiṅgarāya-mahārāya and that they would allot a portion of the land for the midday offerings to god Rāmachandradēva. The land was situated in Agaļi in Rāyadurga-sthaļa which the donor had received for his nāyakatana .

cells.date: Āngīrasa, [Āśvīja] šu. 12, Wednesday = 1512 A.D., September 22.
cells.object: Rock near the temple
cells.remarks: Damaged in the beginning. It states that the dēvādāya and brhamādāya lands under the tank Krottacherūvu, which were held as sarvamānya (free from imposts) from the time of Chikka-ođeya had been reassessed at the time of certain disturbances in the interval. These were once again declared to be free from taxes ( sarvamānya ) by rāyasam Koṇđamarasayya and Dēmarasayya, on the occasion of the pūrṇāhuti of the laksha-hōma ceremony at Penugoṇđa, under the orders of the king, who was then at Šivanasamudram on state business. Kūnama-nāyuđu had this inscription engraved at the instance of those two officers.

cells.date: Śaka 1499, Dhātu, Māgha, śu. 12 = 1577 A.D., January 31, Tuesday The Śaka year was current.
cells.object: On the south wall of the Āñjanēya temple at the north gate of the same fort Telugu
cells.remarks: It states that Savaram Chennappa-nāyaningāru, under orders from Tirumaladēva-mahārāya, was governing Penugoṇḍa-paṭṭaṇa on the 5th day of the bright fortnight of Chaitra in the year Piṅgaļa (1557 A.D., March 5, Friday). It refers to the construction of a minor fort against the bigger fort at Penugoṇḍa, gates, burujulu , moat etc. and also the renovation of the moat of the bigger fort and the durgam fort, for the prowess of Tirumaladēva-mahārāya by Channappa-nāyaningāru. He is stated to have defeated Vaṭmchchika Sarukānu in the month of Pushya of the year Kshaya (1566-67 A.D.) with the aid of Mārakāpura Channarāya of Penugoṇḍa (1568-69 A.D.). It further refers to his victory over the sardārs like Vaṭchina Mālikhān in the month of Vaiśākha of the year Vibhava. Yēdulaśāhi who, came on the first day of the dark fortnight of Mārgaśira of Dhātu (1574 A.D., March 7), conquered the son of a person who claims victory over the Dēva-paṭṭaṇa, etc. created by the god of Penugoṇḍa-paṭṭaṇa.

He is stated to have defeated Vaṭmchchika Sarukānu in the month of Pushya of the year Kshaya (1566-67 A.D.) with the aid of Mārakāpura Channarāya of Penugoṇḍa (1568-69 A.D.). It further refers to his victory over the  sardārs  like Vaṭchina Mālikhān in the month of Vaiśākha of the year Vibhava. Yēdulaśāhi who, came on the first day of the dark fortnight of Mārgaśira of Dhātu (1574 A.D., March 7), conquered the son of a person who claims victory over the Dēva-paṭṭaṇa, etc. created by the god of Penugoṇḍa-paṭṭaṇa.

cells.date: Śaka 1502, Vikrama, Māgha, śu. 15 = 1581 A.D., January 9, Thursday, on which day a lunar eclipse occurred.
cells.object: On a slab set up in the compound of the reading room (the old site of the Kēśavasvāmin temple)
cells.remarks: It states that Chavaram Chennappa-nāyanigāru, son of Chennappanāyani and grandson of Chippagiri Singamanāyani, the ūđigam of Tirumaladēva-mahārāya, while governing the Penugoṇḍa-paṭṭaṇa, under the orders of his overlord, consecrated his family deity Mārakāpuram Chennarāya, built a temple with gōpura and prākāra (circumambulatory path) and conducted the car festival ( ratha-mahōtsava ) in the month of Pushya of Raudri (December, 1580 and January, 1581 A.D.). It refers to the arrangement made by him for the worship of the deity at the time of consecration by the three sthānas of the temple Vōjhula Narasim-bhaṭlu, Rāma-bhaṭlu and Anaṭ-bhaṭlu. Also the karaṇikam given to Jūṭūri Aparasu, for writing the temple accourfts, is recorded. Further it registers the grant of the village Chōlēmari situated to the west of Penugoṇḍa, by Raghunātharājayya at the instance of Tirumaladēva-mahārāju, for the temple. It also records the grant of lands in the village Śunaṅgapuram, Gurijapalle, Lakumādēvipalle, Channāpuram, Raghunāthapuram, Cherukūru, Rāmavojhulapalle, Maṇuthuri, Pedirājupalle-agrahāra for food-offerings, worship and festivals of god at Rāmānujakūṭam for the śrīvaishṇavas , during the tirunakshatra (sacred days) and the five parvas by Śavaram Channappa-nāyuḍu for the merit of the ruler Tirumaladēva-mahārāya and Śrīraṅgadēva-mahārāya.

cells.date: Šaka 1481 (wrong for 1482), Raudri, Māgha, ba. 30 = 1561 A.D., February, 14, Friday when a solar eclipse occurred.
cells.object: Stone near the Narasimha temple
cells.remarks: Records the grant of land in Arakaṭavēmula in Gutti-rājya to gods Rāmēśvara, Ahōbaļēśvara, Veňkaṭādri and Hanumanta for food-offerings, dīpārādhana and parva-tithi-mahōtsavas , by Sōmarasu Peda Tirumalayya. The donor is stated to have obtained the village Arakaṭavēmula from Achyutadēva-mahārāja on a previous occasion. The donor is known to have made a grant of land at Pedda Yekkalūru even as early as Šaka 1436, Yuva (1514-15 A.D.) in the reign of Křishṇadēvarāya, for the merit of Sāļuva Timmarasayya. Cf. No. AP 406 below.

cells.date: Śaka 1437, Yuva, Phālguṇa, śu. 11, Thursday = 1516 A.D., February 14.
cells.object: Stone near the  dhvajastambha  in the Chennakēśava temple
cells.remarks: Begins with a Sanskrit praśasti of the chief Mēsa Timmā-nāyuḍu, son of Chennama-nāyuḍu, belonging to the Vālmīki-vamśa and states that he was holding Kađavakolanu as his nāyaṁkara while mahāpradhāni Sāļuva Timmarasayya was ruling over Gutti-sīma. Records the construction of a śilā-maṇṭapa with prākāra and gōpura , tanks and wells and the laying out of some gardens for the temple of Channakēśava by the chief. Also records a grant of land to some person (name not clear) probably for some service in the temple. It is known from the Kaifiyat of Nađimidođdipālem that Mēsa Chennama took part in Kṛishṇadēvarāya's campaign against Gulbarga and that he received from the emperor, among other things, the titles Aivattāru-maṇđalikara-gaṇđa and Pūrvva-siṁhāsanādhīśvara , the former of which finds mention in the present epigraph.

cells.date: Šaka 1472 (current), Saumya, Šrāvana, ba. 8 = 1549 A.D., August 16, Friday.
cells.object: Slab set up in front of the Chennakēśava temple
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of lands to god Chennakēśava of Niṭṭūru by Rāmalinga-nāyanimgāru, son of Pemmāsani Timma-nāyanimgāru of Niṭṭūru, a village in Chirabađi-sīma, granted to him as umbaļi by Tirumala-nāyanimgāru, son of Jakkampūṇđi Peddi-nayanimgāru of Valluṭla-gōtra, in the nāyaṅkara fief obtained by the latter from Rāmarāja Tirumalarājayyadēva-mahārāja. The gift was made on the occasion of Kṛishṇa-jayanti . The record contains two more grants made on the same occasion, one in the year Kāļayukti (Šaka 1482) by Rāmalinga-nāyuđu and the other in the year Rākshasa (Šaka 1477) by the kāpus (farmers) and karaṇas (accountants) of Niṭṭūr, Gollapalle and Vīmulapalle, the former granting some lands and the latter grain at the rate of 1 mānika for every tūmu of the produce in the village. The record gives an elaborate schedule of assignment of the gift land for various items of offerings during worship, of which one was bhāgavata-sēva and another the chanting of the mantra-pushpam . The two other dates given correspond to 1558 A.D., August 7, Sunday (Šaka 1480) and 1555 A.D., August 10, Saturday, f.d.t. .00. Obviously, the record was put on stone sometime after 1558 A.D., August 7.

cells.object: Stone lying in the ruined fort
cells.remarks: Records a sarvamānya grant of some taxes such as the levy on barbers, kāṇike etc. from Yakkalūru in Penna-māgāṇi attached to Gutti-durga to two ōjus by Śrīraṅgarāju on the orders of Alluđu Rāmarāju and Yaṛa Timmarāju. This Yaṛa Timmarāju is mentioned in the Dēvana Uppalapāđu inscription (No. AP 371 above) as Śrīraṅgarāju Yaṛa Timmarāju and as having received as a grant Jagatāpi-Gutti-sīma. He was a brother of Alluđu (= Aļiya ) Rāmarāju who is also known to have been, like Yaṛa Timmarāju, the son of Āravīđi Śrīraṅgarāju.

text.remarks: Records a  sarvamānya  grant of some taxes such as the levy on barbers,  kāṇike  etc. from Yakkalūru in Penna-māgāṇi attached to Gutti-durga to two  ōjus  by Śrīraṅgarāju on the orders of  Alluđu  Rāmarāju and Yaṛa Timmarāju. This Yaṛa Timmarāju is mentioned in the Dēvana Uppalapāđu inscription (No. AP 371 above) as Śrīraṅgarāju Yaṛa Timmarāju and as having received as a grant Jagatāpi-Gutti-sīma. He was a brother of  Alluđu  (= Aļiya ) Rāmarāju who is also known to have been, like Yaṛa Timmarāju, the son of Āravīđi Śrīraṅgarāju.

cells.date: Šaka 1438, Dhātri, Vaišākha, śu. 3 ( Akshaya-trītīya ) = 1516 A.D., April 5, Saturday.
cells.object: On a stone pillar with a broken Nandi on the top in a field to the west of the canal on the way to Attirāladinne
cells.remarks: Records that Appaya and Gōpaya, sons-in-law of Sāļuva Timmarasu and sons of Nādiņdla Timmarāju, having renovated, at their own cost, the canal named Dēvula-kāluva leading to Timma-samudram named after Timmarasa, created a new village called Lakshmī-samudram in the name of their mother-in-law Lakshmamma, wife of Timmarasu and granted the same on the occasion of akshaya-trītīya to god Bilēšvaradēva of Sajaladiņna for the merit of their grand-parents. Also records an endowment of 5 tūmu of wet land in the newly created village to Ayalōjhala Yara Timmaya for conducting the worship and ēkādaśa-rudrābhishēka every Monday to the deity. The same grant is also recorded in an inscription from Sazzaladinne of the same Taluk. Cf. No. AP 415 below.

cells.date: Śaka 1438, Dhātu, Vaiśākha, śu. 3,  Akshaya-tritīya  = 1516 A.D., April 5, Saturday.
cells.object: Slab lying near the temple of Bilēśvara outside the village
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village Lakshmī-samudram for conducting the daily worship, etc., and periodical festivals to god Bilēśvara at Pennabaḍi Sajjaladiṇne, situated in the Gutti-rājya by Appayya and Gōpayya, sons of Nādimḍla Timmarāja for the merit of Sāļuva Timmarasayya and his wife Lakshmamma. The donors who were the nephews of the famous minister Sāļuva Timmarasa founded the village in the name of the latter's wife and got constructed the garbha-grīha , sukanāsi , antarāla and ranga-maṇdapa of the temple. Cf. No. AP 409 above.

cells.remarks: It registers the remission of taxes on marriages ( peṇđli-sumka ) on married families in Pennabađi-sīma and Gutti-sīma in Gutti-rājya, formerly collected from these families, and grant of the income from tax as sarvamānya on the occasion of Śivarātri , by mahapradhāna Sāļuva Timmayyamgāru, for the merit of the king. cells.reference: MER. , 1892, No. 342;  Ins. Ced. Dits. , p. 134, No. 20;  SII. , Vol. IV, No. 802
cells.object: On the seventh stone in the north-west corner of the courtyard of the same temple
cells.remarks: It records the grant of the village Nedalapāđu renamed as Vīra Narasimħapura by mahāpradhāna Sāļuva Timmayyamgāru, his feudatory, for the merit of the king (Vīra Narasimħarāya-mahārāya), to god Rāmēśvara of Tāđiparati in Pennabađi in Gutti-rājya, for worship, food-offerins, añga-rañga-vaibhava . It is stated that he built bhōga-maṇṭapa , gōpura and prākāra in the temple of Rāmēśvara. It mentions that the gift village Nedalapāđu alias Vīra Narasimħapura in Pennabađi-sthaļa of Gutti-rājya was held by Timmayyamgāru, as a nāyamkara from the king. To this grant, Šrī Rāmachandra, the karta figures as signatory.

cells.date: Šaka 1463, Plava, Āśvayuja, śu. 11 = 1541 A.D., September 30, Friday.
cells.remarks: Wall of the western entrance, left of the Nandi, in the Bugga Rāmalingēśvara temple Records the royal gift of the income from the levy called mahārāja-guttalu from the territory called Gutti-Pennabađi-sīma given to Salakarāju Achchyutarāju for celebrating certain specified festivals to god in the temple of Hampi-Virūpāksham, Tāđiparti and two other places. cells.date: Śaka 1466, Krōdhi, Pushya, ba. 5 = 1545 A.D., January 3, Saturday
cells.object: Stone in a garden belonging to V. Ramachandra
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Ẹanāyani-cheruvu to god Chennakēśava of Vēmulapāḍu in Gutti-sīma for the pāruveṭṭa festival on makara-saṭkrānti day by the vipravinōdins Pina-Gōvindayya and Anamṭayya belonging to Kāśyapa-gōtra, Prathama-śākha and Atharvaṇa-vēda. It is interesting to note that the vipravinōdins in the record claim to belong to the Atharvaṇa-vēda and call themselves as āruvēla-teluṭgalu . It is well known that this class of people practised acrobatics and magic on their profession and their claim to belong to the Atharvaṇa-vēda, which deals with magic and witchcraft, is interesting. An inscription from Kopparti, Cuddapah District ( ARIE. , 1938-39, No. 389) affords another instance of the mention of Atharvaṇa-vēda as the śākha of the vipravinōdins .

cells.date: Śaka 1446, Tāraṇa, Māgha, śu. 7, Monday = 1525 A.D., January 30, Monday.
cells.object: On a rock to the west of the village
cells.remarks: Ref.: A.R.Ep. , 1920, No. 450; SII. , IX, pt. II, No. 516 Records that Lingarasa of Dhārāśura issued orders to the seṭtis , sēnabōvas and local and foreign merchants residing in Velupadige, also called Kṛishṇarāyapura, fixing the rate of taxes in the new bazar street opened in the name of the king as follows: no taxes are to be levied during the first three years; then a varaha per oil-mill, 3 paṇas for a weaving machine; if 10 machines are kept by a single family only nine being taxed; 3 paṇas for a stall; a paṇa for a stall of minor articles - all these to be collected once a year. Velupadige is stated to be the first village of Muda-nāđu belonging to the bhaṇđaravāđa .

cells.date: Śaka 1378, Dhātu, Kaṇṇi, śu. 13, Sunday, Śadayam = 1456 A.D., September 12.
cells.object: On the north wall of the first  prākāra  in the Veñkaṭeśa-perumāļ temple
cells.remarks: Chandragiri This inscription mentions Naraśiṅgadēva-mahārāja as the son of Sāļuva Guṇḍayadēva-mahārāja. It records an endowment by the king of the levies in cash and in kind from the village Alipuram in Vaikuṇḍa-valanādu formerly given by himself as sarvamānya to god Tiruvēṅgaḍamuḍaiyāṇ, for food offerings to the same god during the morning service. It was also laid down that the offering should be utilised for feeding Śrīvaiśṇavas daily at the Rāmānuja-kūḍam, built by the king in Tirumalai Tirupati for his own merit, and presided over by Kandāḍai Rāmānujayyan, disciple of Alagiya Maṇavāla-jīyar.

cells.date: Śaka 1312, Pramōdūta, Mārgaļi 11 = 1390 A.D., December 8, Thursday.
cells.object: On the south wall of the first  prākāra  of the same temple
cells.remarks: It registers an undertaking given by the sthānattar of Tirumala temple of Mullai Tiruvēṅgađa-jīyar, of Aricharaṇālaiyaṇ flower-garden at Tirumala, to provide for the tiruōlakkam daily, on ten days, in the middle of the month of Mārgaļi, for the recital of Tiruppāvai to god Malaikiṇiyaniṇra-perumāļ, Nāchchimār at Tirumala and for the tiruōlakkam daily during the ten days of Tiruppāvai recital and on the occasion of adhyayana festival to god Gōvindarāja-perumāļ, in order to provide for various food-offerings. For this purpose 1200 paṇam was deposited into the treasury. The temple authorities were to supply articles for conducting festivals from the interest against this paṇam . Of the food offered to the god at Tirumala was to be distributed from the donor's share, a portion to Aricharaṇālaiyaṇ-maṭha, and from the remaining of the sthānattār , a portion fo śrīvaishṇavas of Tirupati, to the sabhai of Tiruchchuganūr, to the priest ( nambimār ), to the jīyar of the temple and to the temple accountant who attested this document at the end. It is stipulated that the food offered to god Gōvindarāja-perumāl shall be distributed to the maṭha , which shall receive even after the donor's death ( śarīrāvasāna ) as the maṭha-śēsha-prasādam . The record was written by the kōyil-kaṇakku Tiruniṇrāūr-uḍaiyāṇ. Mullai Tiruvēṅgaḍa-jīyar who figures as a donor in the present record is the same as the one mentioned to have instituted a festival in the name of Harihararāyaṇ in No. 481 below dated in the cyclic year Prabhava, a year before the date of the record under discussion. It is not unlikely, therefore, this record may be assigned to the king Harihararāya.

cells.date: 1310, Āṅgīrasa, Paṅguṇi 2 = 1393 A.D., February 25, Tuesday.
cells.object: On the west wall of the first  prākāra  of the same temple
cells.remarks: It records an undertaking given by the sthānattār of the temple to Mullai Tiruvēngaḍa-jīyar of Aricharaṇālaiyaṇ flower-garden at Tirumala, to provide for food-offerings and lamp to god Malaikiṇiyaniṇra-perumāl and Nāchchimār on the day of vidāyāgri during festivals in the Śrīcharaṇālaiyaṇ maṇḍapa while the deities were seated here, as against the interest for the amount of 600 paṇam deposited into the treasury. It states that the temple treasury should issue a document to the effect of carrying out this gift. It is stipulated that the jīyar should receive 1/4 of the food offered during the tiruōlakkan and 5 nāli and 3 ulakku of food offered to Periya-perumāl. Further, it mentions that the Ēkāki-śrīvaishṇavas belonging to the maṭha should get, even after the death of this jīyar , as śrīcharaṇālāyaṇ-maṭha-śēsha , the food-offering thus made to god. This was attested by Tiruniṇra-ur-veļaiyāṇ, under the instructions of the śrīvaishṇavas .

cells.object: On the east wall of the Baṅgāru-vākili near the twin bells in the Tirumala temple
cells.remarks: It registers an undertaking given by the sthānattār of Tirumala temple to Mādavadāsar alias Mallaṇṇaga! of Chandragiri , disciple of Gōpinātha-ayyaga! , who dug out a channel again at his cost , by desilting it , when the old channel from Madurai river supplying water to the lake at Avilāli , a tiruvīđaiyātṭam of god Tiruvēṅgađam-uđaiyān fell into disuse , connected it to the lake and brought 5000 kulī of land under cultivation and to supply daily the produce , in lieu of the interest for the amount invested by the donor , measured by Malaikiṇiyaniṇrāṇ , for food-offerings to god for a service in his name. It also records a gift of 82 cows for burning 2 perpetual lamps in his name by the same donor , entrusted to the sthānattār to provide for the tiruppeṇagam and lamps. This was signed by Tiruniṇrā-ūr-uđaiyān.

cells.date: Śaka 1355, Pramādi, Vṛiśchika, śu. 10, Sunday, Rēvati-nakshatra = 1433 A.D., November 22.
cells.reference: TTDI. , I, No. 199/89 T.T. and No. 200/162 T.T.
cells.object: On the north wall of the record room verandah in the first  prākāra  of the same temple
cells.remarks: It registers an undertaking given by Tirukkalikaṇṇridāsar, one of the śrīvaishṇavas of Tirupati, the sthānattār of Tirumala to the 24 mahājanas of Agaram alias Śrīnivāsapuram, for the recital of Vēda before god Tiruvēṅgaḍam-uḍaiyāṇ. Since this had been stopped, a representation was made by Tirukkalikaṇṇridāsar to Uḍaiyār Dēvaṇa-uḍaiyār that it should be reinstituted as an endowment of the king Dēvarāya-mahārāya. It states that half of the share of the royal-treasury in Siddhakkuṭṭai in Koṭṭāla-sthaĵa, in Vaikuṇḍa-vaĵanāḍu, which he obtained as śrōtrīya , was granted to the 24 persons, who requested the sthānattār to grant the other half share of the treasury, a sum of 200 paṇam . Tirukkalikaṇṇridāsar arranged for the collection of income from taxes from the tiruvaiḍaiyāṭṭam villages. It is mentioned that the villagers issued a deed to the bhaṇḍāram (treasury), undertaking to collect the amount for the maintenance of these 24 persons and enjoined the two persons to recite before the god.

cells.date: Śaka 1355, Pramādīcha, Vṛischika, śu. 10, Sunday, Rēvati-nakshatra = 1433 A.D., November 22.
cells.object: On the east wall of the  yāgaśāla  in front of  Kalyāṇa-maṇdapa  in the first  prākāra  of the same temple
cells.remarks: It registers a written deed ( muṛi ) issued by the ūravar of the tiruviđaiyāṭṭam villages in Tirukkuđavūr-nāđu and the ūravar of the tiruviđaiyāṭṭam villages in Vaikunđa-vaļanādu to the treasury of the temple of Tiruvēnĝađam-uđaiyān according to which a grant of 200 paṇam as śrōtrīyam for the śrōtrīya-guttugai being the half share of the bhaṇdāra excluding the half share of the bhaṇdāra for the village Siddhanuṭṭai alias Śrīnivāsapuram in Kōṭṭala-sthaļam in Vaikunđa-vaļanādu, for the recital of Vēda before the god Tiruvēnĝađam-uđaiyān on the occasion of Uththāna-dvādaśi by the 24 mahājanas of Śrīnivāsapuram. This was gifted as a charity of the rāya . The villagers of tiruviđaiyāṭṭam villages agreed to remit this amount into the treasury from the year Pramādīcha and the agreement was made so as to enjoin the grant to the mahā-brāhmaṇas of Siddhakuṭṭai alias Śrīnivāsapura as sarvamānya . This document is stated to have been attested by a number of signatories.

text.object: On the east wall of the  yāgaśāla  in front of  Kalyāṇa-maṇdapa  in the first  prākāra  of the same temple
text.remarks: It registers a written deed ( muṛi ) issued by the  ūravar  of the  tiruviđaiyāṭṭam  villages in Tirukkuđavūr-nāđu and the  ūravar  of the  tiruviđaiyāṭṭam  villages in Vaikunđa-vaļanādu to the treasury of the temple of Tiruvēnĝađam-uđaiyān according to which a grant of 200  paṇam  as  śrōtrīyam  for the  śrōtrīya-guttugai  being the half share of the  bhaṇdāra  excluding the half share of the  bhaṇdāra  for the village Siddhanuṭṭai  alias  Śrīnivāsapuram in Kōṭṭala-sthaļam in Vaikunđa-vaļanādu, for the recital of Vēda before the god Tiruvēnĝađam-uđaiyān on the occasion of  Uththāna-dvādaśi  by the 24  mahājanas  of Śrīnivāsapuram. This was gifted as a charity of the  rāya . The villagers of  tiruviđaiyāṭṭam  villages agreed to remit this amount into the treasury from the year Pramādīcha and the agreement was made so as to enjoin the grant to the  mahā-brāhmaṇas  of Siddhakuṭṭai  alias  Śrīnivāsapura as  sarvamānya . This document is stated to have been attested by a number of signatories.

cells.date: Pramādīcha, Kārttigai 25. Probably = 1433 A.D., November 23
cells.object: On the south wall of the same  yāgaśāla
cells.remarks: It registers an agreement made by the ūravar from the tiruviđaiyāṭṭam villages of Kuđavūr-nāđu and Vaikunđa-vaļanādu to the bhaṇdāra of the temple of Tiruvēnĝađam-uđaiyān to remit the sum of 200 paṇam collected from the villages into the treasury, to meet the expenses towards the recital of the Vēda before the god by the 24 mahājanas of Siddhakkuṭṭai alias Śrīnivāsapuram. This document was drafted by Periyanāṭṭu-vēlān under the instructions of ūravar .

cells.object: On the north wall of the kitchen in the first  prākāra  of the same temple
cells.remarks: This inscription contains 4 fragments. The first fragment registers a sale-deed executed by Śaṭhagōpanambi Gōvindaṇ relating to the house-sites and mentions the purchase of a house-site of a certain Dēviyār for 700 narpaṇam . The second one records a transaction of sale made in the Āvaṇakkaļari for the sale of the house-site for 1000 paṇam to the treasury made by Saṭagōpanambi Ālappirandār Gōvindaṇ, who took possession of the property of Perumāl-dēviyār, on the day of Hasta star in the month of Kaṛkāṭaka in the year Pramādīcha. The third fragment records a price-deed ( porulmāvarūdi ) which is also the sale-deed ( selavu-ōlai ) pertaining to the sale of a house-site executed by Saṭagōpanambi Alagippirāṇār Gōvindaṇ for a value of 1000 paṇam along with registration expenses, to the treasury, free from encumbrances. This was attested by Virūppaṇa. The fourth piece refers to the price-deed executed by the Śaṭagōpanambi Gōvindaṇ to the treasury for the house-site sold to the latter free from all encumbrances and this is to be taken as the sale-value. The treasury accepted this price deed which is also sale-deed given with all rights like mortgage, exchange, gift or distribution etc. Vēnkaṭavāṇan figures as a signatory of this record, drafted by Tiruninṇra-ūr-uḍaiyāṇ.

cells.object: On the north wall of the kitchen in the first  prākāra  of the same temple
cells.remarks: This record is in four fragments. The first refers to a purchase from Dēvaṇṇa-uḍaiyār of a house-site for a sum of 2000 paṇam paid into the treasury as kāṇikkai and the sale of three-quarters of a house-site for a price of 450 paṇam . The second piece mentions the setlement of price, entered into the Āvaṇakkaļari . The third records the settlement of a house-site for 1500 paṇam and the sale by Śaṭhagōpanambi Gōvindan to the śrībhaṇdāram of 2 and 3/4 site, with the right to se' or exchange the same. It mentions that the sale-deed was signed by the āchā yapurushas of Tirupati-agaram. Vaḍugavēlān Timmāṇdai of Tiruvēṅgadanallūr and others are referred to as witnesses to this document. In the fourth piece, it is stated that Gövindan executed a sale-deed to the treasury of the temple of Tiruvēngađam-uđaiyān for the sale of 2 and 3/4 site, for the land value of 4200 paṇam , free from encumbrances and the same being entered into the Āvaṇakkaļari . This sale document was drafted by Tiruniṇṇra-ūr-uđaiyān and signed by Aṇṇar Vēngađatturāivār of Kachchiyappāđi, one of the āchāryapurushas of Tirupati-agaram. Appavēlān of Toṇđapāđi, Vennamu-ređđi of Dugga-samudram, Tirumalai-appaṇ, a merchant named Aļagaiyarāyakkāṇ, Periyavēlān, a merchant of Tirupati, Tiruvēngađattaṭtāṇ, Akkappilļai of Tirumaṅgai and Periyap-perumāļ figure as witnesses to this transaction.

cells.object: On the north wall (outer side) of the kitchen in the first  prākāra  of the same temple
cells.remarks: Ends of lines built in. cells.date: Śaka 1356, Ānanda, Karkāṭaka, ba. 11, Friday, Anūrādha-nakshatra = 1434 A.D., July 16.
cells.object: On the door jamb of the Baṅgāru-vākili in the same temple
cells.remarks: It registers an undertaking given by the sthānattār of Tirumala temple to Mudaliyār Tirukkalikaṇridāsar Aṭagappirānār, one of the śrīvaishṇavas of Tirupati, for the amount of 4000 narpaṇam paid into the treasury (by the latter) to meet the expenses to provide for a sandhi in the early morning in his name and also for the daily food-offerings for 6 months from Āḍi to the end of Mārgaṭi in the early morning and worship for the deity. The grains were measured by Malakiṇiyaniṇrān .

cells.date: Śaka 1364, Dundubhi, Māgha, śu. 11 = 1443 A.D., January 12, Saturday.
cells.object: On the wall adjoining the Koppera on the west
cells.remarks: It records the gift of 300 hon during his visit as kāṇike besides 100 hon for various offerings such as garland, food-offerings etc. to god Tirumaladēva by Teppada Nāgeya-nāyaka, son of Muddeya-nāyaka. This gift was enjoined to the sthānattār . Three harivāṇas with symbols and name of the donor were caused to be made in gold and granted to the deity for the specified purpose.

cells.date: Śaka 1366, Raktākshi, Tulā, ba. 5, Friday, Mṛigaśīrsha = 1444 A.D., October 2.
cells.object: On the south wall of the first  prākāra  in Tirumala temple
cells.remarks: It registers an undertaking given by the sthānattār of Tirumala temple to Mallaṇdai, son of Dēvarasar of Chandragiri who excavated a channel from the source in the river Nari for irrigating the achchukkaṭṭu lands in Kōyilēriparṇu in the tiruviḍaiyāṭṭam village Pāḍi, and records that the sthānattār undertook to meet the expenses from out of the yield from this land, measured by Malaikiṇiyaniṇrān , for food-offerings to god Tiruvēṅgaḍam-uḍaiyāṇ during the two sandhis in his name. It is stipulated that the food offered shall be distributed during the sandhi in the pūrva (forenoon) and the remaining share to be utilized during the distribution of the sandhi . Tiruniṇrā-ūr-uḍaiyāṇ figures as a signatory.

cells.date: Śaka 1367, Krōdhana, Dhanus, śu. 14, Monday, Mṛigaśīrsha-nakshatra = 1445 A.D., December 13.
cells.object: On the east wall of the record room in the first  prākāra  of the same temple
cells.remarks: It registers an undertaking given by the sthānattār of Tirumala temple to Emberumāṇār-jīyar, the kōyil-kēl'vi of Pañkayachchelli-tirunandavaṇam at Tirumala, who made a gift of 2000 narpaṇam for two food-offerings along with the daily food-offerings made on the occasion of Bukkarāyaṇ-sandhi to god Tiruvēṅgaḍam-uḍaiyāṇ, from out of its interest. The treasury of the temple undertook to meet the expenses of this endowment from the interest accrued. The food-offerings was to be distributed to the donor, of his share and the remaining to be shared by those who rear the flower-garden.

cells.date: Śaka 1367, Krōdhana, Kumbha, ba. 7, Thursday, Anila (Anusham)-nakshatra = 1446 A.D., February 17.
cells.object: On the west wall in the first  prākāra  of the same temple
cells.remarks: It registers an undertaking given by the sthānattār of Tirumala temple to kōyil-kēļvi Emberumāṇār-jīyar of Pañkayachchelli-tirunandavanam at Tirumala, who made a gift of 1000 narpaṇam , from the interest of which was to be conducted the festivals dvajārōhaṇam from to Chittirai festival to god Tiruvēngaḍamuḍaiyāṇ, Vaikāśi and Āṇi festivals to be celebrated to god Gōvindarāja-perumāļ. It records that from the above interest, the temple treasury should meet the expenses to provide for food-offerings on the occasion of Pushpayagām day during festivals from the beginning of Paṅguṇi every year and for food-offerings to god Gōvindarāja on the occasion of viḍāyārṇi day during Vaikāśi and Āṇi festivals. It states that the food-offerings was made on the occasion of the deity Malaikiṇiyaniṇra-perumāļ and Nāchchimār seated in the maṇḍapa and when the Tiruvāymoļi was recited to god and worship was offered to the goddess Nāchchimār. The food-offerings should be utilised for distribution among the śrīvaishṇavas who recite the Tiruvāymoļi hymns. the Emberumānaḍiyār (temple damsels), to the donor ( jīyar ) and the remaining, after him, distributed among the Ēkāki-śrīvaishṇavas who maintain the Pañkayachchelli flower-garden and the maṭha .

cells.date: Śaka 1368, Kshaya, Mithuna, śu. 3, Monday, Makha-nakshatra = 1446 A.D., June 27.
cells.object: On the north wall in the first  prākāra  of the same temple
cells.remarks: Ref.,: TTDI. , I, No. 221/15 T.T. It registers an undertaking given by the sthānattār of Tirumala temple to kōyil-kēļvi Emberumāṇār-jīyar of Pañkayachchelli-tirunandavanam at Tirumala, who made an endowment of 1000 paṇams paid into the treasury from the interest of which was to be conducted the seven day's festival of dhvajārōhaṇam with the Āṭi-tirunāļ to the Chittirai-tirunāļ to god Tiruvēngaḍam-uḍaiyāṇ, and the two days festivals viz ,, the Vaikāśi and Āṇi tirunāļ to god Gōvindap-perumāļ. in all nine festivals, and provide for food-offerings on the occasion of tirumuļaittirunāļ ( aṅkurārpaṇam ) in his name. The treasury should meet the expenses from the above endowment on the tirumuļait-tirunāļ day, and supply the articles for the sacred-bath to god Malikiṇiyaniṇra-perumāļ, for the worship and food-offerings to the same deity. It is stipulated that the food offered shall be distributed to the donor, a quarter of his share, of 29 nāļi and 3 uļakku and after his death to the Ēkāki-śrīvaishṇavas maintaining the Pañkayachchelli flower garden. Also the food offerings made to god Gōvindap-perumāļ shall be utilised by the donor of his share of 32 nālī , 1 uṛi and 1 ālākku and after him, by the Ēkāki-śrīvaishṇavas of the said garden. Tiruniṇṇra-ūr-uḍaiāan figures as a signatory of the record.

cells.remarks: It registers an undertaking given by the sthānattār of Tirumala to Peri Malladēva-mahārāja, son of Eṇrakampayadēva-mahārāja who is endowed with titles like mahāmaṇdalēśvara , mēdinīmīsara gaṇḍa and Kaṭhāri-Sāṭuva who made a gift of 1000 paṇams paid into the treasury, from out of its interest, to meet the expenses for providing the daily food-offerings to god Tiruvēṅgaḍam-uḍaiyāṇ during the sandhi . cells.date: Prabhava, Āḍi 19 = 1447 A.D., July 17, Monday.
cells.object: On the north wall of the first  prākāra  of the same temple
cells.remarks: It records the gift of 1000 paṇams paid into the treasury to provide for food-offerings to god Tiruvēṅgaḍam-uḍaiyāṇ on the seven festivals, to god Gōvindarāja-perumāl on the two festivals, altogether nine festivals and to goddess Nācchimār on the occasion of abhishēka on the day of Kaiyārchakkaram , from out of the interest on the endowment. The treasury was to meet with the provision for these festivals from the interest accrued from the tirumaļai-tirunāl ( aṅkurārpaṇam ) in accordance with the stone record. The food offered was to be distributed during the tirumaļait-tirunāl-poliyūṭtu-aḍaippu . This was written by Tiruniṇṇra-ūr-uḍaiyāṇ.

cells.object: On the east wall (outer or left side) to the south of the inner  gōpuram  in the second  prākāra .
cells.remarks: Records an agreement between Kandāđi Rāmānujayyaṅgār and the sthānattār of Tirumalai temple whereby the former was authorised to carry out repairs to the damaged and broken jewels, ornaments and gold and silver vessels of Veñkaṭeśa and Gövindarāja, in the presence of the latter, from a capital sum of 3000 paṇam invested by Rāmānujayyaṅgār. This amount he had saved from the income from the villages granted to him by the king, income from šandai makamai and kuttakai levies from Narasingarāyapuram founded by him in the name of the king and other proceeds noted. The king issued a rāyasam to the effect that Kandāđai Rāmānujayyaṅgār was authorised to carry out such repairs from that date. If the expenditure exceeded 3000 paṇam the temple treasury was to meet the extra cost. Both the parties were jointly responsible for supervision of the work.

cells.date: Šaka 1433, Prajāpati, Makara, ba. 10, Anūrādhā, Tuesday = 1512 A.D., January 13.
cells.object: On the west wall of the second  prākāra
cells.remarks: Records the grant of a village made by pradhāni Sāļuva Timmarasayyar, for providing daily tiruppōnakam and atirasapađi to Veñkaṭeśa and Gōvindarāja. He was the Prime Minister and commander of the army of Kļīshṇarāya, married Lakshmī-amman, took prominent part in all Kļīshṇarāya's military campaigns against the Gajapati, king of Orissa, mainly responsible for the capture of Koṇđavīđu, Udayagiri, Koṇđapalli etc., a scholar and commentator upon Agastya's Bāla-bhārata .

cells.object: On the north wall of the first  prākāra  in the 'irumalai temple
cells.remarks: Records details pertaining to a number of ornaments such as uđudhāra , kaṭhāri , padaka , ađđiga , etc., presented by the king to god Tiruvēngaļanātha and the utsavamūrtis (processional images) of the god. cells.date: Śaka 1437, Yuva, Kārttika, ba. 3 = 1515 A.D., October 25.
cells.object: On the north wall of the second  prākāra
cells.remarks: States that the emperor, while staying at Vijayanagara on his return from victorious expeditions presented to god Tiruveñgaļanātha a navaratna-prabhāvaļi . It records his occupation of Udayagiri, Addanki, Vinukonđa, Bellamkonđa, Nāgārjunikonđa, Tañgēđu, Kētavaram and other forts situated on hills and plain, laid siege and captured Koņđavīđu, took alive Vīrabhadra, son of Pratāparudra Gajapati, Narahari, son of Kumāra Hammīra-mahāpatra, Malhi-khān of Rāchūr, Uddaņđa-khān, Janyāla Kasavapātha, Pūsapāti Rāchirāja, Šrīnātha Rāmarāja Lakshmīpatirāja, Paśchima-Bālachandra-mahārāja and other manneyārs (zamindars), granted them their lives and proceeding to Dharaṇikoṭa performed tulāpurusha in the presence of god Amalēśvara on the banks of the Krīshṇavēṇī, made his queens Chinnāji and Tirumala perform mahādānas and returned to Vijayanagara.

cells.date: (1) Šaka 1438, Dhātu, Pushya, śu. 10, Friday = 1517 A.D., January 2
cells.object: On the north wall of the second  prākāra
cells.remarks: (2) Vikrama, Phālguṇa, śu. 11, Sunday = 1521 A.D., February 17. Records the details of the emperor's eastern expedition and states that on returning to the capital Vijayanagara, he paid a visit to the Tirumalai temple and presented to god Tiruvengaļanātha one kaṇḍhamālai (necklace), 30,000 varahas for guilding the vimānam , etc. Further states that, on the second date, the emperor again paid a visit to the Tirumalai temple and presented a pītāmbaram (laced silk cloth) set with nine kinds of precious stones, a kullaya (cap) and two chāmaras and had his queen Tirumaladēvi present a padakam made of nine kinds of stones. He also presented 10,000 varahas as a kāṇuka (tribute) and a valuable padakam . The inscription was engraved by Šrīpati, son of Peddayāsāri, who had accompanied the emperor to the Tirumalai temple, and executed by Bāgūri Mallarasa, the bodyguard ( ūđiga ) of the king. It records his march to Bejwade, occupation of Koṇđapalli, capturing Anantagiri, Unđrakoṇđam, Khānibarimečju, Urlakoṇđa, Aruvapalli, Jallipalli, Kaṇđikoṇđa, Kappaluvāyi, Nallakoṇđa, Kanakagiri, Šaňkaragiri and other forts in Telugu-rājya, plating a pillar of victory at Simhādri Pōṭnūru, performing mahādānas at Rājamahēndravara and return to Vijayanagara on the 1st date when he made gifts also of income from taxes -nityamūlavisan-nāđu , talārikkam and mādārikkam from Tirupati relating to Gođagara-nāđu for morning offerings to god.

cells.object: On the south of the first  prākāra
cells.remarks: Šaka 1436, Bhāva, Makara, śu. 13, Mrigaśīrsha, Friday = 1514 A.D., December 29. Registers the gift of Eṛalapūṇđi village near Vēlumapuram in Māđanallūr-śīrmai for an offering of one tiruppōnakam daily to god Veṇakṭeśa, by Šrīraṅgarāja, son of Rañjakan Tirumalai-nāthar. It is said that Rañjakam Šrīraṅgarāja was the master of a troupe of dancers who were engaged to provide amusement to king Kļishṇarāya who, in due consideration of his talents, conferred upon him the title of Vidvat Sabhārāya Rañjakam . He was a musician and a dancer.

cells.object: On the south wall of the second  prakara
cells.remarks: Śaka 1437 , Yuva , Kanyā , śu. 5 . Anūrādhā , Wednesday = 1515 A.D. , September 12. Records the excavation of a new channel in the Maṇiyakkōnpaṭṭu village , for the merit of the king Kṛishṇarāya , to meet the expenses for certain offerings to god Veṇkaṭeśa in the maṇṭapam constructed by the donor karaṇika Basavarasar , son of Sōmarasar and an officer of king's personal staff , for the merit of the king. The maṇṭapam was in his flower garden to the east of Rāmānuja Puttēri tank on the way to Chandragiri where Vasantōtsava festival was celebrated to the processional deities of Veṇkaṭeśa , Nāchchimār (Padmāvati) and Sēnai-mudaliar (Vishvaksēna).

cells.object: On the west wall of the second  prākāra
cells.remarks: Śaka 1439 , Īśvara , Vṛishchika , śu. 14 , Rōhiṇi , Friday = 1517 A.D. , November 27. Records that Koṇḍu-śeṭṭi , son of Dharmapuram Tomṭmu-śeṭṭi , one of the merchants of Narasiṅgarāyapuram , a sub-area of Tirupati , authorised the collection of income from the second half of the village Chintāyapalli near Vēlumapālam which had been granted to him as vīmbalikai (jāgir) by king Kṛishṇarāya for certain valuable services in the form of supply of provisions of the army , rendered in his military campaign in the south. The first half of the village had already been granted by the donor to god Kālahastīśvara. The temple was to offer duchy-od.nam and appa-paḍi , as stipulated , to gods Veṇkaṭeśa and goddess Padmāvati.

cells.object: On the north wall of the  mēļam  room in the first  prākāra
cells.remarks: Śaka 1439 , Īśvara , Dhanus , ba. 3 , Monday = 1517 A.D. , November 30. Records the payment of 1500 paṇam by Tāllapākkam Tirumalaiyyaṅgār , son of Anṇamaiyaṅgār , the famous musician-poet of the temple , for the daily offering of one tiruppōnakam to the god Veṇkaṭeśa. The Tāllapākkam musician poets were Nadasōka Brāhmaṇas belonging to Bhāradvāja-gōtra, Āśvalāyana-sūtra and ṛik-śākha. Aṇṇamayyaṅgār or Aṇṇayārya was the earliest member of the family. He started composing in his 16th year of age when he had a manifestation of the lord (1424 A.D.) and continued upto 1503 A.D. from whence his son Peda Tirumalāchārya commenced his literary work. Aṇṇayārya continued to sing in the presence of the deity till his 96th year, and must have deceased sometime after the date of his record. His 3 important works are Adhyātma-saṅkīrtanalu , Śriṅgāra-saṅkīrtanālu and Śriṅgāra-maṇjari .

cells.object: On the north wall of the Varadarājasvāmi shrine in the first  prākāra  of Tirumalai temple
cells.remarks: Records the presentation of 360 nāṇpaṇam by Bāhūr Mallarasar or Mallamarāju, one of the personal staff of king Kṛishṇarāya, for providing certain offerings to Malaikuniyaniṇra-perumāl and Gōvindarāja on the days prescribed. The income from the endowment was to be used by the sthānattār for offerings while the deity (processional image) was seated in the maṇṭapam constructed by the donor, on several specified days. 5 paṇam was also to be paid by the temple treasury towards jīvita of the Śrīvaishṇava who was looking after the garden. It is said that the donor accompanied the emperor during his sixth visit to Tirumalai on 16th October, 1518 A.D.

cells.object: On the north wall of the first  prākāra  of the Tirumalai temple
cells.remarks: States that rāyasam Koṇdamarasayyar, son of Timmarasayyaṅgār of Bhāradvājagōtra, Āśvalāyana-sūtra and Rīk-śākhā granted the village Mumbūṇđi in Nallūr-śīrmai of Udayagiri-rājya for conducting services to the deity Tiruvēnkaṭam-uđaiyār. The donor was one of the prominent officers of Krīshṇadēvarāya and took active part in the battle of Raichur. Son of Timmarasa-mantri and Saṅgamāṁbikā, governor of some forts like Ghanagiri and Udayagiri, and a scholar acquainted with the curious writings of 56 countries in india, the hero accompanied the king in the planting of victory pillars at Simhādri and Śrīkūrmam.

cells.remarks: North wall of the first prākāra The cyclic year was Pramāthin. Śaka 1441, Durmati, Mēsha, śu. 14, Hastā, Wednesday = 1519 A.D., April 13. Records an endowment of 2520 nārpaṇam to be used for improvement of irrigation channels of temple villages, by Kandāđai Dođđaiyangār Appai entitled Vēdāntāchārya, son of Venrūmālaiyiṭṭa-perumā! Nāyinār (Śrīnivāsāchārya) of Vādhūla-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra in lieu of which the sthānattārs of the temple were to offer several specified dishes to the processional deity on hearing the Tirumoļi songs of Tirumaṅgaiyāļvār while seated in the shrine of Varāhasvāmi on 40 days. The donor, probably a member of the collateral branch to which śrī Kandāđai Rāmānujayyaṅgār belonged, was residing at Ghaṭikāchala or Sholinghūr. A reputed scholar, known as Mahāchārya or Dođđayyāchārya, he wrote several works like Chaṇđamāruta , a commentary on Śatadūshaṇi of Vēdāntadēśika, Advaitavidya-vijaya , Pārāśara-vijaya , Vēdāntadēśika-vaibhava-prakāśika , Vēdāntadēśika-vimśati etc.

cells.date: Śaka 1442, Vikrama, Vrīśchika, ba. 5, Wednesday, Pūsam = 1520 A.D., November 28, f.d.t. .51
cells.object: On the north wall of the second  prākāra
cells.remarks: Records that Kandāđai Mādhavayyaṅgār, disciple and successor of Kandāđai Rāmānujayyaṅgār, who was the manager of the Rāmānujakūṭams at Tirumalai and Tirupati and the agent of the gold treasury of god Tiruveñkaṭam-uđaiyār, made a gift of 1630 kuļis of wet land of which 1600 kuļis of sarvamānya had been originally gifted by Sāļuva Narasiṁharāya-mahārāya to Kandāđai Rāmānujayyaṅgār and 30 kuļis of land, tank, channels, secured from him by Tirumalai-nāyakkar, and constructed a new village Tirumaladēvipuram, for offerings of different kinds to gods Veñkaṭeśa and Gōvindarājan. A part of the prasādam was to be given to Śrīvaishṇavas chanting the Iyal .

cells.date: Śaka 1443, Vishu, Vrīśchika, śu. 2, Friday, Mūlā = 1521 A.D., November 1, f.d.n. .93
cells.object: On the east wall (outer side) of the shrinē of Varadarājasvāmi in the first  prākāra
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the villages Taṇđalam in Tatvavādi-chēri-śīrmai and Tađapālam respectively by Subuddhi Rāmadāsar and Ambikāmuduśilā, earlier granted to them by Krīsnṇadēvarāya through copper-plate charter, to the deity Veñkaṭeśa at Tirumalai. Subuddhi Rāmadāsar, of Bhāradvāja-gōtra, was the son of Śaṅkaradāsar, while the other donor was the son of Bhīmayar of Kāśyapa-gōtra. Both of them were officers under Gajapatirāya and were taken into service by Kṛishṇarāya who honoured them with dignities and brought them to his allegiance.

text.remarks: Records the grant of the villages Taṇđalam in Tatvavādi-chēri-śīrmai and Tađapālam respectively by Subuddhi Rāmadāsar and Ambikāmuduśilā, earlier granted to them by Krīsnṇadēvarāya through copper-plate charter, to the deity Veñkaṭeśa at Tirumalai. Subuddhi Rāmadāsar, of Bhāradvāja-gōtra, was the son of Śaṅkaradāsar, while the other donor was the son of Bhīmayar of Kāśyapa-gōtra. Both of them were officers under Gajapatirāya and were taken into service by Kṛishṇarāya who honoured them with dignities and brought them to his allegiance.

cells.date: Šaka 1445, Subānu, Makara, ba. 7, Tuesday = 1524 A.D., January 27, Wednesday
cells.object: On the south wall of the second  prākāra
cells.remarks: Records the royal grant of one house-site situated in the north street of the temple at Tirupati, ( TTDI. , III, No. 157) and two sites in the north street of the temple at Tirumalai (See above No. AP 624) to the pontiff Vyāsarāya for building his own maṭhas there. In this connection the record says that the site at Tirupati had been originally granted to a priest but confiscated by the order of Sāļuva Narasimharāya to the temple because of the priest's theft of the temple jewels. Refers to an earlier grant made by the king to god Veṇkaṭēśa of the tax pērāyam to be collected during the Puraṭṭāsi-Brahmōtsava, at Tirumalai, half the village of Kaḍaikūttampāđi and the six villages of Tālļapākkam, Pirāđam, Dārattūr, Muđiyūr, Satrapāđi and Tuṛaiyūr in Pura-maṇđalam (outer division) and arranged a satram to be conducted from his daily share of prasādam which he had authorised the pontiff Vyāsarāya to receive for the charity of his maṭha .

cells.remarks: Śaka 1452, Vikriti, Mēsha, ba. 3, Rēvati, Wednesday. Irregular. The tithi =1530 A.D., April 15, Friday the nakshatra being Anūrādha. Records the cash deposit of 8770 nārpaṇam by Kandāđai Rāmānujayyaṅgār, manager of the gold-treasury of god Veñkaṭēśa and the agent of Rāmānuja-kūṭams, for the occasional offerings to the deities Veñkaṭēśa, Gōvindarāja and Ālīvārs, as his ubhaiyam . This donor is same as Kumāra Rāmānujayyaṅgār, son of Kandāđai Rāmānujayyaṅgār whom Sālīuva Narasimha held in high esteem and appointed as manager of the Rāmānuja-kūṭam at Tirumala and Tirupati. This latter's discipline, Mādhavayyaṅgar was the karta (guardian) of the gold treasury i.e. , jewellery and other gold and silver articles of the temple. After him, the donor of this record also managed the same por-bhaṇdāram .

cells.remarks: Śaka 1454, Nandana, Mēsha, ba. 7, Uttiram, Wednesday = 1532 A.D., March 27 (f.d.t. .14), but the star was Mūla, not Uttiram. Records the grant of two villages, Pūṇdi and Saṅgamakkōṭti in Mēṛai-śīrmai, yielding an annual income of 1000 gold coins, made by Tāllapākam Periya Tirumalayyaṅgār, son of Aṇṇamayyaṅgār, the famous musician-poet of the Veṇkaṭeśa temple, for providing god Veṇkaṭeśa with 40 tiruppōnaka-talīgai , and one atirasa-pađi . Also records the arrangements made for the daily supply of three yagñyōpavītam and 52 rose-water pots during civet-oil oblution to be conducted for the god on 52 Fridays every year. The gift village had been granted to the donor by Achyutarāyá, through a copper-plate grant.

cells.remarks: Tāmil States that the emperor presented a valuable ornament (specified) to god Veñkaṭeśa as his ubhaiyam while he himself was performing the archanā for the god and while the priests ( archakas ) were reciting the Śrīnivāsa-sahasra-nāmam in the presence of queen Varadāji-ammaṇ and her son Kumāra Veñkaṭādri. This is said to have been his first visit more than a year after he went on war with Tiruvađi (Travancore). Cf. Śrī Rājanātha's Achyutarāya-abhyudaya , Cantos 5 and 6. According to this work he is said to have presented a makara-tōraṇa , ear rings, pendants, crown etc.

cells.object: On the north wall of the second  prākāra
cells.remarks: Records that Kandāđai Ariya Rāmānujayyaṅgār paid the sum of 1200 poṇ as the capital for propitiating god Veñkaṭeśa with 2 tiruppōnaka-taļigai and god Gövindarāja with six tiruppōnaka-taļigai daily as his ubhayam . Originally arrangements were made for offering 1 sandhi-tiruppōnakkam and some festival offerings to be made in the name of Śivappu Gövindarāja. Since, for all that 1317 gold coins were estimated (as capital), but only 1200 gold coins were paid by the donor, the last two items were omitted.

cells.object: On the south door-jamb wall (inner side) of  pađikāvali-gōpuram
cells.remarks: Damaged. Speaks of the glory of Tālĵapākkam Tirumalayyaṅgār, son of Aṇṇamaiyyaṅgār, the author of several devotional songs in praise of god Veñkaṭeśa. He is said to have reconstructed the holy tank at Tirumalai with granite steps, and erected the Nīrāļi-maṇṭapam in the midst and built a circumambulatory maṇṭapa around that tank, constructed prākāra walls to the temple of god Varāhasvāmi at Tirumalai, besides erecting the eastern tower for the temple of Veñkaṭeśa. It has been surmised that this record in Tamil poetry must have been composed by the same author.

cells.date: Śaka 1457, Manmatha, DhanuF (Mārgali), śu. 2, Sunday, Tiruvōṇam (Śravaṇa) = 1535 A.D., December 26.
cells.object: On the north wall of the third  /prākāra
cells.remarks: Records that the king inaugurated a festival called Lakshmīdēvī-mahōtsavam to be celebrated for god Tiruveñkaṭam-uđaiyān and Alamelmaṅgai-nāchiyār ( i.e. , Padmāvāti) for 5 days as his ubhayam at Tirumalai. He granted the income, called uttarāyam , of 300 rēkhai-poṇ from the villages situated in the Koṇḍavīḍuśīrmai for the celebration of the same festival. The record specifies the amounts to be spent for preparation of offerings and payments to the temple servants. Of the seven maṇṭapams where the processional deities were to be seated in course of this festival 5 are named after the king, his queen, son (Chikka Veṇkaṭādri), father (Narasa-nāyaka) and mother (Ābalāchchi).

cells.object: On the east, north and west  kumada-paṭtai  of the second of the Tirumalai temple
cells.remarks: Records that Ellappa-pilĵlai, son of Andhakālam-tīrtār, a Gōpāla-śeṭti residing in Tiruvakkarai, paid 700 narpaṇams to the temple treasury for the offering of dadhyōdanam , vellai , tiruvōlakkam , appapađi , etc., to be offered to the deities Malaikuniyaniṇra-perumāl, Nāchchimār and Śēnai-mudaliyār in his garden at Tirumalai in commemoration of the 10th day festival of Chittirai Brahmōtsavam . A supplement added (Nos. 68 of Vol. IV) states that the entire offering is to be distributed freely among the devotees. In the main record it was stated that the donor's share was to be delivered to the Āchchārayyar.

cells.object: On the west wall of the second  prākāra
cells.remarks: Records the sale deed for prasādam offered to god Veñkaṭeśa in the name of Sāluva Timmarasa, son of Rāchirāja, for the sum of 5600 paṇam received, in favour of Tālilipākkam Tirumalayyaṅgār, son of Aṇṇamayyaṅgār, who was to receive the donor's share from the offerings made by Timmarasa's younger brother Gōvindarāja. Sāluva Timmarasa was the minister and commander of the army of Kṛishṇarāya and took prominent part in all of Kṛishṇarāya's military campaigns against the Gajapati king of Orissa and was mainly responsible for the capture of Koṇḍapalli etc. He was a scholar and commented upon Agastya's Bāla-bhārata .

cells.remarks: South wall of the third prākāra Registers a charter in favour of aḍaippam Viśvanātha-nāyaka, son of Nāgama-nāyaka who paid 15000 narpaṇam into the treasury for several offerings to be made to the processional deity seated in the maṇṭapa constructed by him on the bank of the tank of Achyutarāya, on stipulated days. Quarter of the donor's share of appa-prasādam was to be delivered to Uttama Mādhavan, son of Appayan, engaged in repairing the garden maṇṭapam and garden of the donor. The donor was the founder of the Nāyaka dynasty of Madura and served the king earlier as the aḍaippam . He made this grant when he accompanied the king along with other officers like Rāma-bhaṭtar, Salakarāja, Immaḍi Ellappayya and Kṛishṇappa-nāyaka. His father was an able general under Sāļuva Narasimha.

cells.date: Šaka 1458 , Durmukhi , Tai. 1 = 1536 A.D. , December 28.
cells.object: On the west wall of the second  prākāra
cells.remarks: Refers to a sale deed for prasādam offered to god Veňkaťěśa , issued by Sāļuva Timmarasa , for the sum of 1900 paņams in favour of Tāļļapākam Tirumalayyaņgār. In addition to the sold prasādam , the donee (Tāļļapākkam Tirumalayyaņgār) was permitted to collect again a second quarter of the donor's share of various offerings occasionally, like 34 atirasa-pađi , one appa-pađi and vađai-pađi hereditarily. The donee was also empowered to sell, transfer and grant as charity the said prasādam , provided he resides at Tirumalai and offers divine services before god Veňkaťěśa. Širap-pradhāni Sāļuva Timmarasa or Timmaṇa-daṇđanātha had successively served the first three kings of the Tuļuva dynasty viz. , Vīra Narasimha, Krīshṇarāya and Achyutarāya for 30 years until about 1535 A.D. He took a prominent part in Krīshṇarāya's wars against the Gajapati king and the Sultān of Bijāpur. The successful termination of the wars as well as the prosperous rule of Krīshṇarāya are attributable to the wise statesmanship of this able minister Sāļuva Timma.

Širap-pradhāni  Sāļuva Timmarasa or Timmaṇa-daṇđanātha had successively served the first three kings of the Tuļuva dynasty  viz. , Vīra Narasimha, Krīshṇarāya and Achyutarāya for 30 years until about 1535 A.D. He took a prominent part in Krīshṇarāya's wars against the Gajapati king and the Sultān of Bijāpur. The successful termination of the wars as well as the prosperous rule of Krīshṇarāya are attributable to the wise statesmanship of this able minister Sāļuva Timma.

cells.date: Śaka 1460, Viļambi, Tulā, ba. 6, Punarpūśam, Sunday = 1538 A.D., October 13.
cells.object: On the north wall of the third  prākāra
cells.remarks: Records a contribution of 150 chakram-rēkhai-poṇ by Kāļahasti-dīkshitar, son of Nārāyaṇa-bhaṭṭar Upādhyāya-sōmayājiyār of Bhāradvāja-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra, Yajus-śākhā residing at Rayaproli, for providing god Veñkaṭeśa with one tiruppōnakam daily as his ubhaiyam . 1500 narpaṇams was the usual value to be paid in this period for 1 tiruppōnakkam . Hence, it would indicate that this 150 chakram-poṇ herein invested as the capital must be the equivalent amount. Consequently 10 narpaṇam (or paṇam ) would be equal to 1 chakram poṇ which must be the same as 1 gold varaha .

cells.date: Śaka 1465, Šōbhakṛit, Makara, śu. 5, Monday, Uttiraṭṭādi = 1543 A.D., December 31.
cells.object: On the west wall of the third  prākāra
cells.remarks: Records that Kālatti-śeṭṭi, son of Peñgāṇdai-śeṭṭi alias Tiruvēñkaṭamuđaiyan of Peṇṇakka-gōtra, a merchant of Tirupati, inaugurated a festival called Nityōtsavam at Tirumalai for gods Veñkaṭeśa and Varāhasvāmi for a period of 30 days in the month of Tai and Māśi. Another ubhaiyam was also arranged for the god on the day of Mukkōṭi-dvādaśi at Tirumalai for which a sum of 1085 paṇam was deposited by the donor. The reading of the Srīnivāsa-purāṇam was also introduced during the said Nityōtsavam festival.

cells.date: Śaka 1465, Šōbhakṛit, Makara, śu. 11, Saturday, Rōhiñi = 1544 A.D., January 5.
cells.object: On the west wall of the third  prākāra
cells.remarks: Records that Māṭla Varadarāja, son of Pōtarāja and grandson of Māṭla Sōmarāja bearing the titles Kāvēri-vallabha , Okketturā julatalagaṇdu , Gandhagajasimha etc., constructed a maṇṭapam in the garden of his mother Chennamman at Tirumalai and arranged for certain offerings to the utsava-mūrti (processional image) while seated in the above said maṇṭapam during Brahmōtsavam , by depositing the sum of 312 gold coins as his ubhaiyam . The donor is identified with his namesake, son-in-law of Kṛishṇadēvarāya. His wife Kṛishṇamāmbā was the sister of Tirukalāmbā, wife of Aṭiya Rāmarāya. The donor was a Māṭla chief. These are all referred to in the Telugu kāvya 'Kākutstha Vijayamu' by Māṭla Anantarāja, whose patenal uncle the donor was.
