cells.remarks: Records that Mūrti-nāyakkar, son of Kaṭla Koṇđama-nāyakkar of Chaturtha-gōtra, residing in Kumārapalli, granted 4-1/2 shares of lands in Rājēndraśiṅganallūr in Perundi-mānāđu of Pađavū-kōṭṭam with an income of 50 rēkhai and half the village of Pudupaṭṭu Kōnēṭi-kālvāy in Kuđavūr-nāđu with an annual income of 25 rēkhai for certain offerings to be made to the utsava-mūrti Malaikuniyaniṇra-perumāļ and other deities as the ubhaiyam of the donor, his father, mother, wives, younger brother, sons, secretary and other members of his family, on the day of the garden festival, etc. The gift lands were purchased by the donor from Śrīnivāsan, son of Śeruppaṇi Kāśavayyan, for the sake of the donation.

cells.remarks: Records a contribution of 600 paṇam by Šeṇbagavēngu, daughter of Tringēchchelvi Timmi, who was the daughter of Tuṅgā-śelvi, one of the temple-damsels, for providing the god Veñkaṭeśa 10 iđđali-pađi during 10 Chūrṇābhishēkam function (celebrated in Tirumāmaṇi-maṇṭapam - front maṇđapa near Baṅgāru-vākili ), on all the 9th festival days during the Brahmōtsavam as her ubhaiyam . cells.remarks: Records the institution of Kalyāṇa-utsavam for god Veñkaṭeśa for 5 days in the month of Paṅguni through a grant of two villages, Šendalūru in Koṇḍavīđu-śīrmai, yielding an annual income of 500 ghaṭṭivaraha and Mallavaram yielding an annual income of 120 rēkhai-poṇ , by Tālĵlapākkam Tiruvēñkaṭanādha, the fourth son of Tālĵlapākkam Periya Tirumalayyaṅgār who was the son of Aṇṇamayyaṅgār of Bhāradvāja-gōtra, Āśvalāyana-sūtra and Rīk-śākhā. Records also the arrangements made for certain offerings for Alārmēlmaṅgai-nāchchiyār and Varāhasvāmi on the days of hunting festival etc. This donor was the author of a Telugu work Ashṭa-mahishī-kalyāṇamu in Dvipada-metre (published by Tirupati Devasthanam). He was also the author of Paramayōgi-vilāsamu and Ushā-pariṇayamu .

cells.object: On the south and east walls of Varadarāja shrine in the first  prākāra
cells.remarks: It records an undertaking by the sthānattār in Tirumalai given to Hanumayyar Aṇṇaṅgar, son of Lakkappa-nāyakkar, the kilakavar of Māliyavanta (hills) at Vijayanagaram, who made a gift of money for digging the channel excavated in the limits of Kallāru river located below the irrigation tank called Vēňkaṭarāya-samudram (probably named after the ruling king), another channel from the river near the Ālipuram village, and yet another from the Nariyāru river, and granted three-fourth share of the Aṇṇaṅgār-pālaiyam village in the division of the temple villages, from out of its produce yielding an annual income of 365 rēkhai poṇ , excluding the vilūkkāđu (share) of quarter of the lands but along with the rights of irrigation for food offerings to god Tiruvēňgađamuđaiyāṇ and goddess Alarmēlamaṅgai-nāchchiyār, for the merit of the ruling king and queen Kṛishnāji-ammaṇ. The offering was to be distributed to the devotees at the Rāmānuja shrine to Aṇṇāvayyaṅgār, son of Rāmayyar, and to Appāvayyaṅgār, son of Māđabhūsi Aṇṇā with the balance of it set apart for early ađaippu . It mentions that this deed of agreement was prepared with the consent of the śrīvaishṇavas by Tiruniṇrār-uđaiyān, the accountant of the temple.

cells.reference: TTDI. , VI, Pt. I, No. 19/687 T.T.
cells.object: On the east wall, north of  paḍikāval gōpuram
cells.remarks: It records an undertaking by the sthānattār in the Tirumalai temple given to mahāmaṇdalēśvara Chinna Timmarājayyan, son of Chiragiri Rājayyan, grandson of Bhōgaṭa Rājayyan through the agent Tiruvēngaṇa Ayyaṅgār, son of Achyutayyaṅgār, grandson of Abhaiya Narasayyar belonging to Kāśyapa-gōtra, Kātyāyana-sutra and Śukla-Yajuś-śākhā, who made a gift of money for digging out 2 irrigation channels excavated in the village Ilamaṇḍiyan yielding an income of 280 rēkhai-poṇ and 6 paṇam per vaṭṭi of the paddy (produce) to god Tiruvēngaṇamuṇaiyāṇ at Tirumalai, for daily food offerings made in the name of Rāmarājayyan, the avasaram . It was laid down that the offering received as kāṇiyātchi share was to be distributed for feeding the śrīvaishṇavas at the Rāmānuja-kūṭam in Tirumalai and for the maintenance of the life ( śīvidam ) of Gaṭṭu Tiruvēngaṇayyaṅgār of Tirunārāyaṇapuram. Also the food offerings made to god at Tirumalai and god Gōvindarājaṇ on the occasion of Puraṭṭāśi Brahmōtsavam festival and Brahmōtsavam during other months should be utilised for feeding the śrīvaishṇavas who recité the Vēdas ( Adhyayaṇa ). The donor Vijayanagara- Inscriptions. should get his one-fourth share after this distribution to the śrīvaishṇavas and sumaṅgalis (married women). The remaining part of this was to be distributed during the previous adaippu . The document was written by Tiruniṇrāūr-uṭaiyāṇ.

cells.reference: TTDI. , II, No. 30/8 G.T.;  ARSIE. , 1916, No. 762;  SII. , IX, Pt. II, No. 462
cells.object: On the north wall of the central shrine of the Gövindarāja-perumāļ temple Kannada
cells.remarks: Records a royal grant of the three villages Mupaduveṭa and Māṅgođuvelada in Paṭavīđu-rājya and Maṇanūru below the tank of Tirupati stipulating that the worship in the Gövindarāja-perumāļ temple at Tirupati must be conducted on the same lines as those of Tiruvēṅgaļanātha on the Tirumale hill and that Kandāla Rāmānujayya and his pupils should supervise the distribution of the prasāda to Nṛīvaishṇavas , both from outside and local, in the Gövindarāja sannidhi and in the Rāmājuna-kūṭa newly constructed at Tirupati by himself. It also records that the king established a Rāmānuja-kūṭa on the hill and fixed the scale of offerings to god Tiruvēṅgaļanātha to be supervised by the same Kandāla Rāmānujayya and his disciples. Some part of offering (of Tiruvēṅgaļanātha) must be made to the god Aļagiya-perumāļ of Tiruchānūr.

text.remarks: Records a royal grant of the three villages Mupaduveṭa and Māṅgođuvelada in Paṭavīđu-rājya and Maṇanūru below the tank of Tirupati stipulating that the worship in the Gövindarāja-perumāļ temple at Tirupati must be conducted on the same lines as those of Tiruvēṅgaļanātha on the Tirumale hill and that Kandāla Rāmānujayya and his pupils should supervise the distribution of the  prasāda  to  Nṛīvaishṇavas , both from outside and local, in the Gövindarāja  sannidhi  and in the  Rāmājuna-kūṭa  newly constructed at Tirupati by himself. It also records that the king established a  Rāmānuja-kūṭa  on the hill and fixed the scale of offerings to god Tiruvēṅgaļanātha to be supervised by the same Kandāla Rāmānujayya and his disciples. Some part of offering (of Tiruvēṅgaļanātha) must be made to the god Aļagiya-perumāļ of Tiruchānūr.

cells.remarks: South wall (outer side, right of entrance) of the verandah of P.W.D. Store room, opposite Sālai-nāchchiyār's shrine Records a grant of 3180 narpaṇam into the temple treasury by Appa-pillai, son of Karavaṭṭippuliyēļvār of Kauṇđinya-gōtra and Āpastambha-sūtra, a resident of Mahīpālakuļakālachchēri, a part of Rājēndraśōļa-chaturvēdimaṅgalam alias Uttiramērūr for providing offerings on specified days to god Gōvindarāja, while seated in the nīrāļi-maṇṭapam constructed by the donor in front of the kitchen within the temple. The donor, younger brother of Mannār-pilļai, was one of the generals of Vijayanagara forces stationed at Uttaramērūr (in Chingleput District) under Sāļuva Narasimha, Tuļuva Vīra Narasimha and Kṛishṇarāya. Cf. No. AP 842 above.

cells.date: Šaka 1445, Subhānu, Makara, śu. 7, Tuesday, Aśvini = 1524 A.D., January 12.
cells.object: On a slab lying in front of the  Vyasarāya-maṭha  in the Gövindarājasvāmi temple in North Māđa Street, in Tirupati
cells.remarks: Records the authorisation given by the sthānattār of the Tirumalai temple to śīrmai-paramahaṁsa-parivrājakāchārya , padavākya-pramāṇajña , durvādi-garva-sarvasvāpahāra , śrīmat-Vaishṇava-siddhānta-pratishṭhāpanāchārya Vyāsa-tīrtha-śrīpāda to build his own maṭha in a site at Tirupati. The site granted is stated to have been confiscated from a certain Nambi Śīṛṇappaiyar, one of the temple priests for having stolen the temple jewels, by the order of Sāļuva Narasimharāya-mahārāja. Also states that Vyāsa-tīrtha was entitled to receive the donor's share of the prasādam offered in the name of the king.

cells.object: On the right door-jamb wall (inner side) of the first  gōpuram  known as  paḍikāvali-gōpuram  of the Rāmasvāmin temple at Tirupati
cells.remarks: States that Kumāra Rāmānujayyaṅgār constructed a wooden car for god Raghunāthan for the merit of the king vīrapratāpa Vira Achyutarāya-mahārāya. cells.remarks: Records the gift of lands purchased from Malainiṇra-perumāl, son of Narasayya for 3500 paṇam and made over, along with other wet lands, into the temple treasury by Rāmā-bhaṭtar, son of Bhūtanātha Śishṭabhaṭtar of Chandragiri in Vaikunda-vaļanāđ, for providing certain offerings and conducting Panguṇi-Uttiram festival to god Gövindarājan and floating festival to god Rāma. cells.date: Śaka 1460, Viļambi, Tulā, ba. 2, Wednesday, Krīttikai = 1538 A.D., October 9
cells.object: On the east base (outer side) right of entrance of the first  gōpuram  in the same temple
cells.remarks: Ref.. TTDI. , IV, No. 112/148 G.T. Registers an agreement between the cloth and yarn merchants of Toṇđai-maṇđalam, Puṇa-maṇđalam and Uļa-maṇđalam on one side and the lease holders of Vijayanagaram, Magadhapaṭṭaṇam, Vidurapaṭṭaṇam and Pūranappūr, regarding weaving of cloths. It is laid down that in the course of weaving by handloom 1/3 of śađiserakkuvađam (commonly known as achchukaṭṭu ) should be drawn lengthwise and 2/3 of cotton should be used in cross-wise weaving, and that this mode of weaving should be done only by the Muslims. Further states that a fine of 12 gold varaham will be imposed upon any one violating this rule and paid into the temple treasury of god Veñkaṭēśa.

Rāyasam  Koṇđamarasayyar, the donor, was a capable military officer and first general of Udayagiri fort, soon after its capture by Kṛishṇarāya on 1514 A.D., June 9.

cells.remarks: Records that mahāmaṇđalēśvara Aliya Rāmarājadēva-mahārāya, son of Āravīđu Bukkarāja Śrīraṅgarāja granted, for the merit of the emperor, Pudupaṭṭu in Neydal-aṇđai (division) in Ārya-śirmai yielding an annual income of 200 rēkhai-poṇ for the purpose of conducting the mukkōṭi-dvādaśi festival, daily worship and other services to gods Veñkatēśa and Gōvindarāja as his ubhaiyam . It was stipulated that Veñkaṭatturāivār, son of Vađamāmalai-ayyan and Anantayyaṅgār, son of Tiruvēñkaṭayyan were to be paid for reciting Tiruvēñkaṭa-mahātmyam at Tirumalai and Tirupati respectively at the rate of 6 and 4 paṇams per month.

cells.remarks: It records an undertaking given by the sthānattār of the temple at Tirumalai to Periya Timmappa-nāyakkar of Chaturtha-gōtra belonging to Kavaṛai community and Vjayanagaram, who granted the village Agaram Pūndamalli in Pālaiya-śirmai in Terku-māgāṇai yielding an annual capital income of 320 rēkhai-poṇ paid into the temple treasury for food offerings during the festivals conducted to god Gōvindarāja and Rāmānuja at Tirupati. It is also stipulated that from out of the food offerings made to god on the occasion of Adhyayanōtsavam celebrated for Rāmānuja, on the occasion of Brahmōtsavam to god Gōvindarāja and goddess Śuđikuđutta-nāchchiyār, pūvōlat-tirunāļ (flower decoration festival), tuļasi-māhātmyam tirunāļ and vasantōtsavam (spring festival) shall be distributed to Siddhayan Bhūlōkan and Periya Perumāļ-jīyar and the remaining was to be set apart for distribution during early ađaippu .

cells.object: On the south wall of the second  prākāra  of the same temple Tamil, Tamil and Grantha
cells.remarks: Damaged and incomplete. It registers an undertaking given by the sthānattār of the temple at Tirumalai to Nārāyaṇa-dāsari-nāyakkar , who granted the income of 600 rēkhai-poṇ from the village Timmāpuram in Chandragiri-rājya for various food offerings to gods Raghunātha and Gōvindarāja on specified festive occasions. It also records the gift made by Gōvindappar Kṛishṇayyaṇ to god for food offerings on the occasion of tiruppalṭi-eṭuchchi to the same god and during the celebration of Kārtigai Rāmanavami , Vaikāśi Brahmōtsavam , Muchukunda-mōksham festival and to the deity Paṭṭābhi Veṅkaṭeśa-perumāl installed by him. The temple accountant Malaiyappaṇ is stated to have granted the income of the interest amount ( poli-ūṭṭu ) to god Paṭṭābhi Veṅkaṭeśa-perumāl on the occasion of Chittirai-Vishu festival and to god Gōvindarāja on the occasion of Kārtigai and Vaikāśi tirukkoḍi-tiruṇāl , Māśi-Makham and Paṅguṇi-Uttiram festivals. It was also arranged to donate from out of the interest income , food offerings to goddess Śūḍikkoḍutta-nāchchiyār (Āṇdāl) on the Mārgaṭi-nīrāṭṭam festival day in th temple of Gōvindarāja.

cells.remarks: Registers an endowment of 440 rēkhai-poṇ through excavating irrigation channels in the villages (name lost) of Koḍavūr-nāḍu in Uļa-maṇdalam by Nōṭṭakāra Nārāyaṇan, son of Noṭṭakāra Veñkaṭayyan and grandson of Kōnappayyan residing in Daṇṇāyaka-maṅgaļam, a village established by Veñkaṭapatidēva-mahārāya, for providing certain offerings to the god at Tirumalai on specified occasions. The donors, of Bhāradvāja-gōtra, Āśvalāyana-sūtra and Ēik-śākhā, were nōṭṭam officers (i.e., estimators of jewels and other valuables) under 3 generations of rulers. The king is identified with Rāma II, son of Śrīraṅga II who was the son of Rāma I, the elder brother of Veñkaṭa I under whom Rāma II served as his co-regent and himself ascended the throne in 1614 A.D.

cells.remarks: It registers an undertaking given by the sthānattār of Tirumalai temple to Aṇṇaṅgarāchārya, son of Aļagarajāyyaṅgār and grandson of Prativādi-bhayaṅkaram Veṅgaṇāchari of Śrīvatsa-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra and Yajuś-śākhā of Ayyaṅgār-tiruvīdhi alias Śrī Bhāshyakārar-agrahāram in Tirupati who made a grant of 25 rēkhai-poṇ for the land for digging out the Lakshmīnārāyaṇa-perumāļ channel on the occasion of the consecration of Lakshminārāyaṇa-perumāļ, for the disilting and renovation of the Gōpiļayyan channel in the village Avilāli, and made another grant of 150 kulī of wet-lands and 18 rēkhai-poñ for digging out a channel-all these yielding an annual income of 348 rēkhai-poñ and 8 pañam , for conducting the nine different festivals and for food offerings in the name of Prativādi Bhayaṅkaram Aṇṇaṅgarāchāri of Tirupati, to god Gōvindarāja-perumāļ, goddess Nāchchimār, Kṛishṇan, Lakshmīnārāyaṇa-perumāļ and Rāma.

cells.date: Śaka 1438, Īśvara, Tulā, śu. 14, Monday. Irregular. 1517 A.D., September 28, Wednesday. The Śaka year was 1439.
cells.object: On the north wall of the  maṇđapam  in the Śiva temple
cells.remarks: It records an agreement among the merchants, Ayyāvaļi Pekkaṇdār of the Fifty-six countries and the different tradesmen from several countries carrying on their profession in Nāvalan-perunteruvu at Puttalai-paṭṭu in Paļuvūr-kōṭṭam of Toṇđai-maṇđalam, fixing the rate of magamai dues payable by them to the temple of Bhīmiśvaram-uđaiya-nāyinār of the place, on the different articles of merchandise. The magamai dues are to be paid on cattle, cotton, yarn, cloth, wool, areca-nut, pepper, silk yarn, oil, cummin seed, sesamum, jaggery, salt, turmeric, sugar, ghee, buffalo, rice and ginger.

cells.date: 15th regnal year, Subhakṛit, Mēsha, śu. 5, Wednesday, Rōhiñi = 1362 A.D., March 30
cells.object: On the east and north bases of the Mrītyuñjayēśvara shrine in the Kāļahastīśvara temple
cells.remarks: It registers a gift of 3 cows and a bull for a perpetual lamp to god Tirukkāļatti-uđaiya-nāyaṇār of Tirukkāļatti alias Mummuđiśōļapuram in Ārĵrūr-nāđu in Jayaṅgonđaśōļa-manđalam by Pichchiyākkam-uđaiyān Vilāđarāyan Sōnamā[da*]dēvan. The gift was entrusted to the shepherds of this temple. Mudaliyān, son of Nārpatteṇṇāyirakkōn Dēvagaļ, and his heirs undertook to supply 1 uļakku of ghee daily measured by Tirukkāļatti-uđaiyān measure for maintaining the above lamp.

cells.remarks: It registers the gift of 400 paņam out of the income received from the sale of land at the rate of 4 paņam per 100 kuļi of land measured by Tirukkāļatti dēvadāna measuring rod by Chikkaraśar, son of Mādi-araśar Ayyalu Peggađaiyār, for the service to god Tirukkāļatti-uđaiya-nāyanār, in their name. cells.date: Šaka 1432, Pramōda, Karkaṭaka, śu. 10 = 1510 A.D., July 16, Tuesday
cells.object: On the north base of Mrītyuņjēśvara shrine in the same temple
cells.remarks: It registers a gift of 800 paņam by Dukkaņar Pichchappilļai of Vēlaņjēru made over to the śrībhaņdāra kankāņi of the temple of Tirukkāļatti-uđaiya-nāyanār at Tirukkāļatti alias Mummađiśōļapuram, for digging out pits in the lake called Mantiri-kuļam at Chiṭṭātūr, a dēvadāna of the temple for irrigating the lands below it, to provide for food-offerings during the early morning service, for the supply of a flower garland, for the burning of a lamp, in the day, before the shrine and for the maintenance of 4 lamps, daily, in the night, from out of the income from the lands thus brought under cultivation. It was entrusted to Kailāyam-uđaiyār and his descendants to conduct the gift. This document was attested by Maruttavan Tūlī-Ālīvān Periya-uđaiyān of a place (name not clear). An amount of 2 paṇam annually is mentioned to have been apportioned for the distribution in the village among the ūravar probably accrued from out of this garden.

cells.date: Śaka 1438, Dhātri, Pushya, śu. 13, Monday = 1517 A.D., January 5
cells.object: On the west wall of the second  prākāra  of the same temple
cells.remarks: The record is important for the historical portion contained in it. The king, it is stated, started out from Vijayanagara on a campaign of conquest towards the east, conquered Udayagiri fort, Addamki, Vinikomḍa, Bellamkoṇḍa, Nāgārjunakomḍa, Tamgēḍa, Kētavaram and other hill-forts, land forts and captured Rāutarāya-mahāpātra. Having taken Komḍavīḍu, he captured alive Vīrabhadrarāya, son of Pratāparudra Gajapatirāya, Naraharidēva, son of Kumāra Hamvīrapātra, Rāchūri Mallū-khānu, Uddamḍa-khānu, Jamnyāla-Kasavāpātra, Pūsapāti Rāchīrāju, Śrīnātharāju, Lakshmīpatirāju, Paśchima-Bālachamdra-mahāpātra and others. Later, he reinstated the captives in their places, visited Amarēśvara at Dharanikōṭa, performed the tulāpurusha ceremony, returned to Vijayanagara, and started out on a campaign of conquests towards Kaliṅga, reached Bejavāḍa, conquered Komḍapalli fort, captured alive Praharāju Śiraśchandra-mahāpātra, Boḍajana-mahāpātra, Bipli-khānu and others, took the fortresses of Telamgāṇya like Anamtagiri, Umḍrakomḍa, Urlugomḍa, Aruvapalli, Jallipalli, Kamḍikomḍa, Kappaluvāyi, Nallagomḍla, Kambhammeṭtu, Kanakagiri, Śamkaragiri etc., installed the jayastambha at Simhādri-Poṭnūru and performed the mahādāna there, returned to Rājamahēndra, returned to Vijayanagara and having visited, on the above date, with his queens Chinnādēvi and Tirumaladēvi to perform the mahādāna before god Kālahastīśvara at Kālahasti where he had the 100-pillaredmahādāna and the last entrance big gōpuram . This epigraph was written by king's ūḍigaṇ Mallarasa and Rāyasaṇ Śrīpati.

cells.date: Śaka 1469, Plavaṅga, Makara, śu. 15, Tuesday, Pushya = 1548 A.D., January 24, f.d.t. .05
cells.object: On the south wall of the second  prākāra  of the same temple
cells.remarks: It records a gift of 100 paṇam paid into the treasury, by the son of Deviyaṅgaļ-perumāļ of Paramēśvaramaṅgaļam and the accountant of Nārāyaṇapuram in Vaṭṭiūr-nāḍu in Kuṇravattanak-kōṭṭam, for the excavation of a lake in the dēvadāna village of the deity, for providing irrigation facilities to the lands brought under cultivation and from the income ( mudal ) of which to meet the annual expenditure for food offerings on the fourteen festival days to god Šōļaviṭaṅkar, for the coating of the image, with camphor and for taking out the image on procession in the street, in the temple of Tirukkāļatti-uđaiya-nāyaṇār of Tirukkāļatti alias Mummuđi-šōļapuram in Ārĵrĵr-nāđu in Jayaṅgonđašōļa-manđalam. The food offering was to be received by the heirs of Dēvaṇar-gurukkaļ, son of Ayyap-piļļai Kuppayyar, a śaiva chakravarti .

cells.date: Šaka 1475, Prāmādi, Mīna, ba. 11, Wednesday, Tiruvōṇam = 1554 A.D., February 28; f.d.t. .16
cells.object: On the south and east bases of Mrītyuñjayēśvara shrine in the same temple
cells.remarks: It registers a gift of 100 paṇam by a native of Paramēśvara-maṅgaļam, an accountant of Nārāyaṇapuram in Vaṭṭi-ūr-nāđu in Kuṇrāvarttanak-kōṭṭam, which was received by the śrībhaṇdāra kaṅgāṇam of the temple of Tirukkāļatti-uđaiya-nāyaṇār, at Tirukkāļatti alias Mummađiśōļapuram in Ārĵrĵr-nāđu in Jayaṅgonđa-šōļa-manđalam, for the excavation of a lake in the dēvadāna village Bhasavapuram, in order to bring the lands under cultivation, and the income of which was assigned to provide for tiruvālattitaṭṭam and food-offerings to god Imaiyōrgaļ-nāyagar, before the balipīṭha at the entrance of the temple, on the seventh day festival in the month of Māśi. The articles for food-offering was to be supplied, measured by śrībhaṇdārakkāl . It is stipulated that the above food-offerings was to be distributed among Sadāśiva-gurukkaļ, son of Dēvappar-gurukkaļ, the temple accountant and the adhikāri and his heirs, according to their respective shares.

cells.date: Śaka 5[6]9[0], Śārvari (wrong), Vaiśākha, śu. 15. Irregular.
cells.object: On the copper-plates received from C.F. Brackenbury, esq., I.C.S., Special Settlement Officer
cells.remarks: The king is, perhaps, to be identified with Tirumala I, brother of the famous Rāmarāja (Hemrāj). Registers that two Ređdis came from the sea-side country, with their cattle and children to the village Rāvulakollu and got permission to construct a village near the hill, from Yara-Timmarāja who was then governing Ghanđikōṭa. Its boundaries are defined and service-inams settled. The grant was written by Teliki Bāla-baṭuđu. But the record does not appear to be genuine.

cells.date: Śaka 1403, Prajāpati, Māgha, Śukla-dvādaśi = 1572 A.D., January 26, Saturday
cells.object: On the copper-plates received by the Special Settlement Officer
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village Penugulūru alias Yellamarājasamudram, together with the two hamlets Yelammapāđu Chennapalli and Koñđūru-Chennapalli, made by the king, at the request of the Małla chief Timmarāja, to a number of Brāhmaṇs. The granted village is situated on the eastern bank of the Mahābāhu in Pottapa-nāđu, of Siddhavarta-śīma. The entire village was divided into 128 vṛittis and given to 115 brāhmaṇas who were highly learned in the śāstras and were masters of the Vēdānta. Besides these, one vṛitti was granted for the study of the Rīgvēda, one for that of the Yajurvēda and one each to the local shrine of Vishṇu and Hara.

cells.date: Śaka 1432 [Pramōda], Kārtika, śu. 12= 1510 A.D., October 14, Monday
cells.object: Rock in a field to the south of the village
cells.remarks: It states that marriages in the several communities of Karṇāṭa had been withheld for payment of peñdli-suñkam (marriage taxes) and that on the representation of Tippana, son of Nāgināyamāguru and others(names lost), the said tax was exempted from payment by all communities of Karṇāṭi-sīme. The representation was made to the king, by pradhāni Sālūva Timmarasayya, Ādeppa-nāyaka and others. The damaged record refers to Penugoṇđa-rājya, Būmukoṇđa-sthaļam and Rangasamudaram-agrahāra.

cells.date: Šaka 1481, Siddhārtin, Šrāvaņa, ba. 12, Friday. The  tithi  = 1559 A.D., July 31, Monday
cells.object: On a rock in the village
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of wet and dry lands to god Lakshmī-narasiṁha at Rāmagiridurga by Jillēļa Veņgaļayyadēva-mahārāju, son of Krīshṇamarāju and grandson of Peda Krīshṇamarāju of Kāśyapa-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra, Yajus-śākhā. The gift lands are stated to be situated in Vempalapalli in the village of Mudivāđa in Vāvilipāṭi-sīma belonging to Rāmagiri-durga of Penugoņđa-mārjavāđa which the donor is said to have obtained as amara from Rāmarāju Tirumalarājayyadēva-mahājāju. Daņđapalle Ref. EI., XIV, No.2 On the copper-plates received from the maṇegar Sanskrit and Kannada in Nandināgari Saṅgama; Vijaya-Bhūpati (prince Bukka III) Vikṛiti, Bhādrapada, śu. 1, [ēkādaśī], Śrāvaṇa, Lakshmīnārāyaṇa-yōga = 1410 A.D., September 10. Records the gift of the village Kṛiyāśaktipura in Daṇdēhalĵi-sthaḥa, in Hulu-nāḍu of Muļvāgila-rājya, to Kṛishṇa-paṇḍita, son of Mēchāmbikā and Śiṅgaṇārya, of Bhāradvāja-gōtra. The donee constructed a tank, Vijaya-samudra, in the granted village (Kriyāśaktipura) and having secured the permission of the king, dividing the village into 82 vṛittis , granted the village and the tank to a number of brāhmaṇas of different gōtras . The grant was made by the king in the honour of the Śaiva teacher Kāśīvāilāsa Kriyāśakti. Mentions the name of the king's mother as Dēmāmbikā, daughter of Nūka-bhūpāla of solar race.

cells.remarks: North, west and south walls of the central shrine in the Kalyāṇa-Veñkaṭēśa-perumāl temple Records that a certain Virupaṇṇa founded a town called Veñkaṭādri-samudram on the borders of Nārāyāṇapuram and constructed there the temple of Veñkaṭādri-perumāl for the benefit of Veñkaṭādrirāya-mahārāya and for offerings, with the permission of the king, made a gift of some complete villages and shares in others.

cells.date: Śaka 134 [9], Plavaṅga = 1427-28 A.D.
cells.remarks: East wall of the maṇđapa in front of the central shrine of Chidambarēśvara temple Built in. Mentions the Śaiva and Vaishṇava shrines of Chandragiri-rājya, like Kāñchipuram, Tirukkālatti, Tiruvarṅriyūr, Tiruvālāngāđu, Tiruppālaivanam etc. Refers to vibhūtikālatti , collected in the temple of Alagiyatiruchchirṅrambalam-uđaiya-nāyaṇār at Sattirapāđu, in Maṅgalūru-nāđu of Kuṇṅravattaṇa-kōṭṭam in Jayaṅgoṇđa-śōla-maṇđalam and to certain royal orders ( rāyasam ) issued to Ariyappa-daṇṇāyaka, Bhiksāvṛitti-ayyagaļ and Dēvarāya-ođeyār of Chandragiri.

cells.remarks: Records that vidvan-mahājanas , the village officials and mahāmaṇdalēśvara Rāmarāju Kōnēṭi Timmarājayyadēva-mahārāja agreed among themselves that the levy of grain at a specified rate collected on all the lands in the village be utilised for maintaining the tanks, ponds and the canals of the village in the proportion of the irrigated areas under each of them.

cells.date: Śaka 1377 ( dhātu adri-guṇa-bhū ), Yuva, Kārttika paurṇami, Monday = 1455
cells.remarks: Ref.: Set of 3 copper-plates kept in the office of the Director of Epigraphy A.D., October 25. But the weekday was Saturday. Prince Triyambaka, son of Dēvarāya II and elder brother of Immađi Prauđha-dēvēndra (Mallikārjuna) while governing Ghanādri (Penugoṇđa) province, gifted the village Bommenālū, renaming it as Lakshmīpura (after the name of his mother), to the brahmin, Māchivōkta, son of Vallabhōkta of Śukla-Yajuś-śākha. This is a palampsist reengraved over a record of Vikramāditya II of the Eastern Chālukya family.

cells.date: Śaka 147[8], Naļa, Jyēshṭha śu. 15 = 1556 A.D., May 24, Sunday on which day a lunar eclipse occurred.
cells.object: Slab set up in front of the Hanumān tēmple
cells.remarks: Registers the village Kūđlūru alias Ređđirājapuram comprising also the hamlets (?) Kāṭepalle and Muddalāpuram, as a sarvamānya agrahāra by mahāmaṇdalēśvara Rāmarāju Viṭhalarāju Tirumalayyadēva-mahārāja, to the learned scholars. The donor had received Rāyadurga-sīma, in which the gift village was situated, from the king as nāyaṅkara . The latter portion of the inscribed slab is damaged and from the extant portion it would appear the gift was made a month earlier on Vaiśākha śu. 15.
